description: Curated, source-verified Courtside Archive game recaps. Player tokens use the same canonical College Baseball player IDs rendered by player.html.

paragraphs: [[cb-san-diego-roman-garcia|Roman Garcia]] put San Diego in front in the first with an RBI groundout that scored [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]].

San Diego broke the game open with four runs in the third. [[cb-san-diego-roman-garcia|Garcia]] singled in his second run, [[cb-san-diego-kevin-collard|Kevin Collard]]’s sacrifice fly brought home [[cb-san-diego-riley-adams|Riley Adams]], and [[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]] capped the inning with a two-run single for a 5–0 lead.

[[cb-san-diego-nick-sprengel|Nick Sprengel]] carried a shutout through eight innings, allowing five hits and striking out seven. Back-to-back seventh-inning doubles by [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Schuyler]] and [[cb-san-diego-riley-adams|Adams]] made it 6–0 before [[cb-byu-colton-shaver|Colton Shaver]] hit a three-run ninth-inning homer; [[cb-san-diego-troy-conyers|Troy Conyers]] retired the final three hitters for the save.

[[cb-california-jared-horn|Jared Horn]] opened California’s 2018 season with five scoreless innings, escaping a fifth-inning threat with runners on second and third by striking out the final two hitters.

California finally broke through in the sixth when [[cb-california-andrew-vaughn|Andrew Vaughn]] singled home the game’s first run. A patient five-run eighth followed, built on a hit batter, five walks and two singles to turn the pitchers’ duel into a 6–0 lead.

[[cb-california-jared-horn|Horn]] allowed four hits, walked two and struck out six to earn the win, while the bullpen covered the final four innings for the save. San Diego scored once in the eighth, but California finished an 8-hit, 6–1 opening-night victory.

[[cb-california-andrew-vaughn|Andrew Vaughn]] delivered a 5-for-5 afternoon with a double, two home runs, five RBI and two runs. His first two-run homer tied the game at 4–4 in the third, then he singled home another run in the sixth as California took a 6–4 lead.

San Diego’s answer was a seven-run seventh. [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]] tied the game with a two-run double, then [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] and [[cb-san-diego-jeff-houghtby|Jeff Houghtby]] delivered run-scoring singles as the Toreros surged ahead 11–6.

[[cb-california-andrew-vaughn|Vaughn]] homered again in the eighth to trim the margin, but [[cb-san-diego-gabriel-ponce|Gabriel Ponce]] earned the win with two innings of relief and [[cb-san-diego-justin-friedman|Justin Friedman]] finished the 11–8 San Diego victory.
[[cb-cincinnati-kyle-mottice|Kyle Mottice]] put Cincinnati ahead in the first with a solo home run, then delivered an RBI single in the second after California had briefly tied the game.

California drew even on its second-inning double-and-triple sequence, but Cincinnati answered immediately. [[cb-cincinnati-kyle-mottice|Mottice]]’s single restored the lead, and [[cb-cincinnati-manny-rodriguez|Manny Rodriguez]] added a fourth-inning solo homer for the decisive 3–1 margin.

[[cb-cincinnati-jt-perez|J.T. Perez]] earned the win with five innings of one-run ball and five strikeouts. [[cb-cincinnati-david-orndorff|David Orndorff]] then covered the final three innings without allowing a run, striking out three for the save.

[[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]] gave San Diego the first run with a first-inning RBI single, but [[cb-cincinnati-cole-murphy|Cole Murphy]] answered with a three-run homer in the second to put Cincinnati ahead.

San Diego chipped back, first on a fourth-inning RBI single and then with two eighth-inning runs. [[cb-san-diego-garrett-calvert|Garrett Calvert]]’s RBI groundout and [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]]’s sacrifice fly tied the game at 4–4.

Cincinnati broke through for three in the 10th: [[cb-cincinnati-manny-rodriguez|Manny Rodriguez]] hit a sacrifice fly before [[cb-cincinnati-treg-haberkorn|Treg Haberkorn]] lined a two-run single. [[cb-cincinnati-jarod-yoakam|Jarod Yoakam]] worked 1.1 scoreless innings for the win, and [[cb-cincinnati-reese-robinson|Reese Robinson]] struck out two in a clean 10th for the save.

[[cb-cincinnati-connor-mcvey|Connor McVey]] went 2-for-3 with two walks as Cincinnati built a 3–0 lead through six innings, with [[cb-cincinnati-aj-bumpass|AJ Bumpass]], [[cb-cincinnati-manny-rodriguez|Manny Rodriguez]] and [[cb-cincinnati-cole-murphy|Cole Murphy]] each driving in a run.
San Diego used a two-run sixth to pull within 3–2, then [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]] posted the game’s biggest offensive line at 3-for-4 with two runs and three RBI.

The Toreros scored twice in the ninth to complete the 4–3 walk-off. [[cb-san-diego-travis-kuhn|Travis Kuhn]] held Cincinnati scoreless over two relief innings, allowing two hits and one walk while striking out two to earn the win.
[[cb-cal-poly-kyle-marinconz|Kyle Marinconz]] opened Cal Poly’s second inning with a single, then [[cb-cal-poly-nick-meyer|Nick Meyer]] doubled him home for the game’s first run.

Arkansas tied it in the fourth on [[cb-arkansas-heston-kjerstad|Heston Kjerstad]]’s RBI groundout. Cal Poly used an error-assisted two-run seventh to take a 3–1 lead, but [[cb-arkansas-dominic-fletcher|Dominic Fletcher]] answered with a two-run homer to tie it again.

[[cb-cal-poly-blake-wagenseller|Blake Wagenseller]] singled as a ninth-inning pinch hitter, and [[cb-cal-poly-alex-mckenna|Alex McKenna]]’s RBI single restored the lead. [[cb-cal-poly-andrew-alvarez|Andrew Alvarez]] then earned the win with 1.1 perfect innings and two strikeouts.

[[cb-san-diego-adam-kerner|Adam Kerner]] opened the third with a double, moved to third on a wild pitch and scored on [[cb-san-diego-trevor-rosenberg|Trevor Rosenberg]]’s RBI single. After a sacrifice bunt and another wild pitch, [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]] singled home Rosenberg for a 2–0 San Diego lead.

San Diego created breathing room in the seventh when [[cb-san-diego-kevin-collard|Kevin Collard]] tripled and pinch-runner [[cb-san-diego-chris-colarossi|Chris Colarossi]] scored alongside Kerner on Otsuka’s two-RBI single. Michigan scored on an eighth-inning double-play ball, but Colarossi’s RBI single in the bottom half restored the four-run margin.

[[cb-san-diego-paul-richan|Paul Richan]] carried the Toreros through eight innings, limiting Michigan to three hits and one run while striking out nine. [[cb-san-diego-justin-friedman|Justin Friedman]] struck out two in a perfect ninth to finish the 5–1 victory.

[[cb-cal-poly-kyle-marinconz|Kyle Marinconz]] scored Cal Poly’s first run in the second on [[cb-cal-poly-nick-meyer|Nick Meyer]]’s safety squeeze bunt, but Grand Canyon’s pitching kept the Mustangs off the board from there.

Grand Canyon moved ahead in the fifth after [[cb-grand-canyon-tyler-wyatt|Tyler Wyatt]]’s bunt single and [[cb-grand-canyon-griffin-barnes|Griffin Barnes]]’ sacrifice bunt set up back-to-back RBI singles by [[cb-grand-canyon-marc-mumper|Marc Mumper]] and [[cb-grand-canyon-channy-ortiz|Channy Ortiz]]. Ortiz added a seventh-inning sacrifice fly after another Wyatt single and Barnes bunt.

[[cb-grand-canyon-quin-cotton|Quin Cotton]] started the eighth with a single, and [[cb-grand-canyon-preston-pavlica|Preston Pavlica]] followed with a two-run homer. [[cb-grand-canyon-mike-lundin|Mike Lundin]] worked six innings of two-hit, one-run baseball, while the bullpen combined for three scoreless frames in the 5–1 win.

[[cb-grand-canyon-quin-cotton|Quin Cotton]] scored the first run of a four-run Grand Canyon fourth, and sacrifice flies by [[cb-grand-canyon-zach-malis|Zach Malis]] and [[cb-grand-canyon-marc-mumper|Marc Mumper]] kept the inning moving. [[cb-grand-canyon-channy-ortiz|Channy Ortiz]] singled home another run before [[cb-grand-canyon-pikai-winchester|Pikai Winchester]] doubled in the fourth run.

San Diego answered immediately. [[cb-san-diego-adam-kerner|Adam Kerner]] walked in a run, [[cb-san-diego-jeff-houghtby|Jeff Houghtby]] lined a two-run single, and [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]]’s RBI groundout completed a four-run tie. The Toreros then broke it open in the eighth as Kunst and [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]] drove in runs before [[cb-san-diego-daniel-gardner|Daniel Gardner]] singled home two.

[[cb-san-diego-louie-crow|Louie Crow]] erased the Grand Canyon offense over three hitless innings, allowing two walks and striking out three. [[cb-san-diego-travis-kuhn|Travis Kuhn]] followed with two perfect innings to earn the win as San Diego completed the 8–4 comeback.

Arkansas struck first with three runs in the second. [[cb-arkansas-casey-opitz|Casey Opitz]] singled home [[cb-arkansas-carson-shaddy|Carson Shaddy]], then [[cb-arkansas-jax-biggers|Jax Biggers]] doubled in Opitz and [[cb-arkansas-jared-gates|Jared Gates]] for a 3–0 lead.

San Diego immediately made up ground when [[cb-san-diego-tyler-herburger|Tyler Herburger]] launched a two-run homer in the third after [[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]]’s leadoff single. The Toreros took control with five in the fifth: [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]] singled in the tying run, [[cb-san-diego-daniel-gardner|Daniel Gardner]]’s sacrifice bunt put them ahead, and [[cb-san-diego-kevin-collard|Kevin Collard]] and Bewley added RBI singles.

Arkansas cut the margin to one with a seventh-inning [[cb-arkansas-eric-cole|Eric Cole]] RBI single and [[cb-arkansas-grant-koch|Grant Koch]]’s two-run pinch-hit single in the eighth. [[cb-san-diego-justin-friedman|Justin Friedman]] closed the ninth in order for the save, finishing San Diego’s 7–6 win.

[[cb-arizona-ryan-haug|Ryan Haug]] scored Arizona’s first run in the fifth when [[cb-arizona-alfonso-rivas|Alfonso Rivas]] hit into a double play, and the Wildcats held that 1–0 lead into the bottom of the sixth.

San Diego turned the game with three unearned sixth-inning runs. [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]] singled home [[cb-san-diego-daniel-gardner|Daniel Gardner]], [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]] added a sacrifice fly, and [[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]] drove in Otsuka. Two more runs followed in the seventh as [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] and [[cb-san-diego-adam-kerner|Adam Kerner]] scored on wild pitches before [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]] delivered a sacrifice fly.

Arizona pushed across late runs on [[cb-arizona-nick-quintana|Nick Quintana]]’s RBI double and [[cb-arizona-cameron-cannon|Cameron Cannon]]’s RBI single, but [[cb-san-diego-louie-crow|Louie Crow]] recorded the final two outs for the save. [[cb-san-diego-nigel-ward|Nigel Ward]] earned the win with two scoreless relief innings.

[[cb-indiana-scotty-bradley|Scotty Bradley]] opened the scoring with a second-inning RBI groundout, then Indiana erupted for five in the fourth. [[cb-indiana-ryan-fineman|Ryan Fineman]] doubled in two, [[cb-indiana-matt-gorski|Matt Gorski]] and [[cb-indiana-jeremy-houston|Jeremy Houston]] added RBI grounders, and [[cb-indiana-logan-kaletha|Logan Kaletha]] singled home the sixth run.

Fineman kept the pressure on with a two-run fifth-inning homer, giving him three hits, four RBI and two runs. San Diego answered with one in the fourth and three in the sixth, including [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]]’s sacrifice fly, [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]]’s sacrifice fly and [[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]]’s RBI double.

Indiana rebuilt its cushion in the eighth on [[cb-indiana-matt-lloyd|Matt Lloyd]]’s two-run double. [[cb-indiana-jonathan-stiever|Jonathan Stiever]] earned the win with 5.2 innings and seven strikeouts, while [[cb-indiana-kade-kryzsko|Kade Kryzsko]] allowed one hit across 3.1 scoreless innings for the save.

[[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]] opened the first by scoring on [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]]’s RBI groundout, then [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]] singled home [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] and [[cb-san-diego-adam-kerner|Adam Kerner]] doubled in [[cb-san-diego-daniel-gardner|Daniel Gardner]] for a 3–0 lead.

Indiana chipped away on [[cb-indiana-matt-gorski|Matt Gorski]]’s fourth-inning RBI triple and [[cb-indiana-elijah-dunham|Elijah Dunham]]’s RBI single, but San Diego made it 6–1 in the fifth. [[cb-san-diego-garrett-calvert|Garrett Calvert]] singled home Gardner, [[cb-san-diego-jeff-houghtby|Jeff Houghtby]] lifted a sacrifice fly, and Kunst’s RBI single brought in Kerner.

[[cb-san-diego-chris-murphy|Chris Murphy]] struck out seven over six innings to earn the win. Indiana pulled within one in the ninth on [[cb-indiana-matt-lloyd|Matt Lloyd]]’s two-run double after [[cb-indiana-luke-miller|Luke Miller]]’s eighth-inning homer, but [[cb-san-diego-louie-crow|Louie Crow]] closed out the save.

[[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]] opened Game 2 with a first-inning homer, then drove in [[cb-san-diego-jeff-houghtby|Jeff Houghtby]] with a third-inning triple. Houghtby later hit a solo homer in the fifth and added an RBI double in the sixth as San Diego built a 5–2 lead.

Indiana’s [[cb-indiana-logan-kaletha|Logan Kaletha]] kept answering. He singled home [[cb-indiana-drew-ashley|Drew Ashley]] in the third, tripled home Ashley and [[cb-indiana-jeremy-houston|Jeremy Houston]] in the seventh to tie it, then singled home the go-ahead run in the ninth.

[[cb-indiana-matt-lloyd|Matt Lloyd]]’s sixth-inning homer started the late charge, and the Hoosiers added a tying RBI single in the ninth before Kaletha’s decisive hit. Indiana completed the 6–5 comeback after trailing by three runs.

[[cb-san-diego-adam-kerner|Adam Kerner]] scored the game’s first run in the second on [[cb-san-diego-jeff-houghtby|Jeff Houghtby]]’s RBI fielder’s choice, but Indiana answered in the third when [[cb-indiana-matt-lloyd|Matt Lloyd]] drove a three-run homer to right, bringing home [[cb-indiana-logan-kaletha|Logan Kaletha]] and [[cb-indiana-jeremy-houston|Jeremy Houston]].

Indiana broke it open with three more in the fifth. [[cb-indiana-matt-gorski|Matt Gorski]] singled home [[cb-indiana-logan-sowers|Logan Sowers]] and [[cb-indiana-luke-miller|Luke Miller]], then stole second as [[cb-indiana-ryan-fineman|Ryan Fineman]] stole home. Gorski added an RBI double in the seventh and finished 4-for-5 with three RBI.

San Diego pushed across two unearned runs in the eighth, including [[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]]’s RBI single, but Indiana held on 8–4. Indiana’s starter earned the win after allowing one earned run in four innings.

San Diego carried a 2–0 lead into the sixth at Fowler Park, with [[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]] driving in one of the early runs. San Diego State then flipped the game with seven runs in the inning on three hits, small ball and Torero miscues, turning the tight crosstown game into a 7–2 Aztec lead.

[[cb-san-diego-state-jordan-verdon|Jordan Verdon]] went 2-for-4 with a double and two RBI for San Diego State, while [[cb-san-diego-state-dean-nevarez|Dean Nevarez]] added two hits and two RBI. Nevarez’s RBI double in the seventh made it 8–2 before [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]] answered with an RBI single for San Diego.

[[cb-san-diego-state-daniel-ritcheson|Daniel Ritcheson]] earned his first collegiate win, allowing one unearned run over two innings in relief. [[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]] went 2-for-5 with an RBI in the 9–3 loss.

San Diego answered [[cb-santa-clara-andre-nnebe|Andre Nnebe]]’s first-inning RBI double with two runs of its own: [[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]] singled home [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]], then [[cb-san-diego-daniel-gardner|Daniel Gardner]] brought [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]] home with a sacrifice fly.

[[cb-santa-clara-jake-brodt|Jake Brodt]] tied the game with an RBI double in the third, and [[cb-santa-clara-evan-haberle|Evan Haberle]]’s RBI single put the Broncos ahead in the sixth. Brodt homered in the eighth as Santa Clara used a six-run inning to turn its one-run lead into a 9–2 advantage.

[[cb-santa-clara-austin-reyes|Austin Reyes]] supplied the finishing touch with a three-run homer in the ninth. [[cb-santa-clara-penn-murfee|Penn Murfee]] earned the win with five scoreless innings of relief, allowing one hit and striking out six.

[[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]] walked, took second on a wild pitch and scored on [[cb-san-diego-daniel-gardner|Daniel Gardner]]’s first-inning RBI single. Gardner delivered again in the fifth, singling home Otsuka and [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]] before [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] added a sacrifice fly.

Gardner finished 3-for-4 with the first three San Diego RBI. The Toreros added four in the eighth as [[cb-san-diego-adam-kerner|Adam Kerner]] walked in a run, [[cb-san-diego-tyler-herburger|Tyler Herburger]] doubled home two and Kunst drove in the final run on a groundout.

[[cb-san-diego-chris-murphy|Chris Murphy]] overwhelmed Santa Clara for eight innings, allowing one hit while striking out 14. The Broncos scored twice in the ninth after Murphy departed, but San Diego closed out the 8–2 series-evening win.

San Diego scored first when [[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]] drove in [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]] with a first-inning groundout, but Santa Clara took over in the second. [[cb-santa-clara-jason-dicochea|Jason Dicochea]] delivered a two-run single before [[cb-santa-clara-jake-brodt|Jake Brodt]] cleared the bases with a three-run double.

The Broncos added five more in the third, capped by [[cb-santa-clara-andre-nnebe|Andre Nnebe]]’s three-run homer. Nnebe finished with two hits and four RBI, while Brodt matched him with four RBI on two hits as Santa Clara built a 10-run lead through five innings.

[[cb-santa-clara-joe-becht|Joe Becht]] homered twice and scored three times, helping Santa Clara finish with 16 runs on 15 hits. Bewley homered and drove in three for San Diego, but [[cb-santa-clara-travis-howard|Travis Howard]] earned the win with 5.1 innings of three-run work.

UC Irvine took a 1–0 first-inning lead and protected it into the eighth, turning the midweek matchup into a pitching duel. [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]] finally tied it with his fourth homer of the season, a solo shot in the bottom of the eighth.

The Toreros had their best chance in the ninth, loading the bases with two outs, but the inning ended on a flyout. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-collard|Kevin Collard]] went 2-for-4 for San Diego, while Schuyler finished 2-for-5 with the game-tying homer.

In the 11th, [[cb-uc-irvine-matt-reitano|Matt Reitano]] hit the deciding homer for the Anteaters. [[cb-uc-irvine-evan-mcmillin|Evan McMillin]] earned the win with two innings of one-hit relief and Cole Spear recorded the save in UC Irvine’s 2–1 victory.

Loyola Marymount opened the scoring in the first and added two more in the fourth, carrying a 3–1 lead into the sixth. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-collard|Kevin Collard]] supplied San Diego’s first run with a second-inning solo homer.

[[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]] brought the Toreros even in the sixth, driving a two-run homer to left after [[cb-san-diego-daniel-gardner|Daniel Gardner]] reached base. The 3–3 tie held through eight innings.

LMU broke through in the ninth on a sacrifice fly, then Tyler Cohen worked two scoreless innings of relief for the win. [[cb-san-diego-paul-richan|Paul Richan]] gave San Diego seven innings of three-run, seven-strikeout work before the late loss.

[[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]] and [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] set the table for San Diego’s three-run first, with Otsuka scoring on a passed ball before [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]] singled in McGuire and [[cb-san-diego-jeff-houghtby|Jeff Houghtby]] doubled home Schuyler.

Schuyler’s second-inning double drove in Otsuka and McGuire before he came home on an error, extending the lead to 6–0. LMU answered with three in the third, but [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|McGuire]] and Schuyler added RBI hits in the bottom half to restore the cushion.

San Diego kept tacking on runs as [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]], [[cb-san-diego-daniel-gardner|Daniel Gardner]] and [[cb-san-diego-connor-doyle|Connor Doyle]] each drove in a run. [[cb-san-diego-chris-murphy|Chris Murphy]] earned the win, and [[cb-san-diego-gabriel-ponce|Gabriel Ponce]] covered the final four innings scoreless for the save.

Loyola Marymount jumped ahead 2–0 in the first, but [[cb-san-diego-kevin-collard|Kevin Collard]] immediately tied it with a two-run double. Collard singled home another run in the third, while [[cb-san-diego-connor-doyle|Connor Doyle]] reached on an error for an RBI and [[cb-san-diego-jeff-houghtby|Jeff Houghtby]] drove in two more as San Diego took a 7–2 lead.

[[cb-san-diego-connor-doyle|Connor Doyle]]’s two-run homer in the fourth pushed the advantage to 9–2. After LMU trimmed the gap to four in the fifth, Collard doubled in two, Doyle was hit by a pitch with the bases loaded and Houghtby launched a grand slam to break the game open.

Houghtby finished 2-for-5 with a homer and six RBI, while Collard went 3-for-6 with five RBI. [[cb-san-diego-travis-kuhn|Travis Kuhn]] earned the win with 4.1 innings of one-run relief as San Diego completed the 18–6 series-clinching rout.

Saint Mary’s scored once in the second, but San Diego moved in front with one run in the fourth and two in the fifth. [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]] doubled in two runs and [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]] went 3-for-4 for the Toreros.

The Gaels broke it open with five runs in the sixth, turning a 3–1 deficit into a 6–3 lead. [[cb-saint-mary-s-kevin-milam|Kevin Milam]] contributed two hits and two runs while also taking the ball for Saint Mary’s.

San Diego rallied within a run on a pair of seventh-inning runs, but [[cb-saint-mary-s-andrew-hansen|Andrew Hansen]] retired all four batters he faced before [[cb-saint-mary-s-michael-hobbs|Michael Hobbs]] secured the final inning. Milam earned the win after allowing five runs over 6.1 innings.

Cal State Fullerton built a 4–0 lead through four innings, but [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]] and [[cb-san-diego-connor-doyle|Connor Doyle]] scored on [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]]’s two-run single to start San Diego’s six-run fourth.

[[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] singled home Schuyler, [[cb-san-diego-jeff-houghtby|Jeff Houghtby]] drew a bases-loaded walk, and Otsuka singled home two more to give the Toreros a 6–4 lead. [[cb-san-diego-adam-kerner|Adam Kerner]] later doubled in two runs in the sixth.

[[cb-san-diego-anthony-donatella|Anthony Donatella]] erased the Fullerton offense with 3.2 scoreless innings and five strikeouts in relief. San Diego added an unearned run in the fifth and three in the sixth to finish a 10–4 comeback.

[[cb-gonzaga-nick-brooks|Nick Brooks]] opened a five-run second with a two-run homer, then [[cb-gonzaga-isaac-barrera|Isaac Barrera]] doubled in a run and [[cb-gonzaga-ernie-yake|Ernie Yake]] singled home two.

San Diego answered with [[cb-san-diego-adam-kerner|Adam Kerner]]’s RBI double and [[cb-san-diego-jay-schuyler|Jay Schuyler]]’s RBI single, but [[cb-gonzaga-branson-trube|Branson Trube]] broke it open with a two-run sixth-inning single and a two-run homer in the eighth.
Yake capped Gonzaga’s 17-hit attack with a two-run ninth-inning double, while [[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]] homered in the bottom half. Gonzaga took the opener, 13–3.
[[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] doubled home a first-inning run and [[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]] added another on a fielder’s choice as San Diego jumped ahead 2–0.

Gonzaga answered with an unearned run in the fourth, then [[cb-gonzaga-gunnar-schubert|Gunnar Schubert]] delivered a three-run double in the fifth. [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]] answered with a solo homer, but the Toreros could get no closer.

[[cb-gonzaga-alek-jacob|Alek Jacob]] earned the win with 5.1 innings, and [[cb-gonzaga-casey-legumina|Casey Legumina]] struck out five across three scoreless innings for the save. Gonzaga took the 5–3 decision despite San Diego’s 10 hits.
[[cb-san-diego-brhet-bewley|Brhet Bewley]] opened the scoring with a sixth-inning homer, and [[cb-san-diego-nate-kuchta|Nate Kuchta]] carried a 1–0 lead through six innings while allowing one run.

Gonzaga struck for four in the seventh, with [[cb-gonzaga-isaac-barrera|Isaac Barrera]] and [[cb-gonzaga-ernie-yake|Ernie Yake]] driving in runs before [[cb-gonzaga-gunnar-schubert|Gunnar Schubert]]’s two-run single made it 4–1.

UC Irvine pushed across its only run in the fourth when [[cb-uc-irvine-sam-ireland|Sam Ireland]] singled home a run. San Diego’s bullpen then shut the door over the final five-plus innings.

[[cb-pacific-nate-verlin|Verlin]] finished 2-for-4 with five RBIs as Pacific piled up 19 hits in a 16–7 win. Reyes went 2-for-4 with three runs and two RBIs for San Diego.

[[cb-san-diego-travis-kuhn|Travis Kuhn]] earned the win with 3.1 scoreless relief innings, allowing two hits and striking out four. San Diego’s bullpen held Pacific scoreless after the fourth.

San Diego took a 2–0 first-inning lead when [[cb-san-diego-stephen-dubb|Stephen Dubb]] drove in an unearned run and [[cb-san-diego-max-jung-goldberg|Max Jung-Goldberg]] followed with an RBI single. [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] added an RBI double in the second.

[[cb-san-diego-nathan-walker|Nathan Walker]] worked the ninth for his second save, striking out two. San Diego held on for the 5–4 victory.

[[cb-san-diego-adam-lopez|Adam Lopez]] opened the scoring with a two-run double in the first, then [[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] singled home two more in the third. [[cb-san-diego-adam-kerner|Adam Kerner]] added an RBI single as San Diego built a 5–0 lead.

[[cb-san-diego-grady-miller|Grady Miller]] held UC Irvine scoreless through six innings, allowing two hits and striking out six. After the Anteaters scored in the eighth, [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] answered with a solo homer.

[[cb-iowa-grant-leonard|Grant Leonard]] finished the game for his second save as Iowa won 4–1. [[cb-arizona-donta-williams|Donta Williams]] had two of Arizona’s four hits.

[[cb-san-diego-michael-dixon-ii|Michael Dixon II]]’s RBI single started a four-run third for San Diego, followed by RBI singles from [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] and [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]]. Seattle answered with a solo homer in the fourth.

[[cb-seattle-alex-mcbee|Alex McBee]] earned the win as Seattle finished with 15 hits in a 9–2 victory. Maningo went 2-for-4 with two RBIs and a run.

[[cb-san-diego-jake-miller|Jake Miller]] threw a no-hitter, walking two and striking out 10 in the 7–0 victory. [[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] supplied three hits in San Diego’s nine-hit offense.

[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Ricketts]] finished 3-for-5 with two RBIs, including the walk-off single in the tenth. San Diego completed the 4–3 comeback.
[[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] drove in three runs and [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 5-for-5 with two RBIs as San Diego built an 11–0 lead through six innings.
[[cb-san-diego-max-jung-goldberg|Max Jung-Goldberg]] collected three hits and two RBIs, while [[cb-san-diego-adam-kerner|Adam Kerner]] added two hits and an RBI.

[[cb-san-diego-max-jung-goldberg|Jung-Goldberg]] went 1-for-3 with the game’s key RBI double. San Diego won 2–0.

San Diego opened the series at Tony Gwynn Stadium with two first-inning runs, as [[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] reached on an RBI error and [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]] followed with an RBI single. The Toreros added two more in the fifth to trim the deficit to one.

The Toreros stretched the margin with three fourth-inning runs, including [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]]’ RBI double and [[cb-san-diego-adam-lopez|Adam Lopez]]’s sacrifice fly. [[cb-san-diego-jake-miller|Jake Miller]] earned the win after allowing two runs, one earned, across five innings.

UC San Diego scored first, but San Diego answered with [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]]’s RBI single in the second and four runs in the third. San Diego broke the game open with four runs in the eighth, capped by [[cb-san-diego-adam-lopez|Adam Lopez]]’s three-run double. Lopez finished 2-for-4 with four RBI in the 10-2 victory.

San Diego and UC San Diego traded early runs before the Toreros took control with three in the fourth. San Diego’s eighth-inning burst began with [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]]’s RBI double before Luevano launched a three-run homer. [[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] finished with four RBI.
UC San Diego opened with two first-inning runs, sparked by [[cb-uc-san-diego-jackson-kritsch|Jackson Kritsch]]’s RBI double. The Tritons held that 2-0 advantage into the seventh.

Santa Clara flipped the game with four runs in the seventh. [[cb-santa-clara-ryan-mccarthy|Ryan McCarthy]] hit a two-run homer, and [[cb-santa-clara-eamonn-lance|Eamonn Lance]] went 3-for-3 with two runs in the 6-4 win.

UC San Diego pulled within two on [[cb-uc-san-diego-anthony-lucchetti|Anthony Lucchetti]]’s eighth-inning homer, but [[cb-santa-clara-locke-bernhardt|Locke Bernhardt]] earned the win with 2.1 relief innings and five strikeouts before the Broncos closed it out.

San Diego answered an early UC Riverside lead with [[cb-san-diego-adam-lopez|Adam Lopez]]’s two-run double in the third, then added three in the fourth as [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] doubled home a run and Lopez drove in two more.

[[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] broke the game open with a two-run homer in the fifth and a three-run homer in the sixth. He finished 3-for-4 with three runs and five RBI as the Toreros built an 11-2 lead.

San Diego added five more in the eighth to finish a 16-4 win, with [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] contributing an RBI single. [[cb-san-diego-jake-miller|Jake Miller]] earned the win, striking out 10 over six innings while allowing two runs, one earned.
San Diego took a 3-0 lead in the third when [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] doubled home two and [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] followed with an RBI single.

The Toreros added four eighth-inning runs. [[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] tripled in a run, [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]] singled home another, and [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]] doubled in two.

[[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] struck out 12 while allowing two hits over seven scoreless innings, and [[cb-san-diego-kieran-shaw|Kieran Shaw]] finished the two-hit shutout for a 7-0 victory.

In the second game, San Diego put up four first-inning runs, beginning with [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]]’s two-run homer. [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] added an RBI double as the Toreros took immediate control.

[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] hit a solo homer in the fifth, and [[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] followed with a two-run shot in the sixth. San Diego added another run on [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]]’s sacrifice fly in the seventh.

[[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] worked five no-hit innings with nine strikeouts, while [[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] closed the combined two-hit shutout over the final four frames. The Toreros completed the sweep with a 9-0 win.

San Diego answered an early UC Riverside lead with solo homers from [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] and [[cb-san-diego-adam-lopez|Adam Lopez]] in the fourth, but the Highlanders moved ahead 4-2 with three runs in the fifth.

The Toreros started their comeback on [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]]’s RBI single in the seventh, then tied it in the ninth when Kunst brought home [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] with a sacrifice fly.
In the 10th, Jefferis drew a bases-loaded walk to force home the winning run and lift San Diego to a 5-4 victory. [[cb-san-diego-kieran-shaw|Kieran Shaw]] earned the win with a scoreless 10th inning.

San Diego erased a 5-1 fifth-inning deficit at USC. [[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] doubled home two in the sixth, and [[cb-san-diego-adam-lopez|Adam Lopez]]’s seventh-inning RBI single pulled the Toreros within a run.

The Toreros took the lead in the ninth on [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]]’s RBI double and [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]]’s RBI single. [[cb-san-diego-carter-rustad|Carter Rustad]] earned the win in relief.
Costello finished a perfect 5-for-5 and drove in the game’s decisive insurance run. [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]] added two hits as San Diego completed the 6-5 comeback at Dedeaux Field.
[[cb-san-diego-jake-miller|Jake Miller]] set the tone for San Diego with 10 strikeouts over 4.2 innings, allowing one unearned run, as the Toreros beat Pacific 3–1 at Fowler Park.

Pacific scored its only run in the second, but [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]] answered with a solo homer in the third. [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] singled home the go-ahead run in the sixth, and [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] doubled in Kunst in the seventh.

[[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] earned the win with 1.1 scoreless innings, and [[cb-san-diego-kieran-shaw|Kieran Shaw]] retired all seven hitters he faced while striking out four for the save.

paragraphs: [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] went 4-for-4 with a double, a home run, three runs and four RBIs as San Diego routed Pacific 15–3 at Fowler Park.

The Toreros struck for six runs in the first two innings, with [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]] opening the scoring on a solo homer and McGuire following with a three-run blast. [[cb-san-diego-adam-lopez|Adam Lopez]] added a two-run homer, while [[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] drove in three.

[[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] finished 4-for-4 with three runs, and the San Diego staff held Pacific to three unearned runs: [[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] worked 4.2 innings before [[cb-san-diego-jack-hyde|Jack Hyde]] earned the win with 2.1 scoreless innings.
[[cb-san-diego-adam-lopez|Adam Lopez]] went 3-for-3 with a double and two RBIs as San Diego beat Pacific 5–1 to complete the series at Fowler Park.

Pacific led 1–0 after a first-inning homer, but Lopez doubled in [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] and [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] in the third. The Toreros added three in the fifth on [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]]’ sacrifice fly, a wild pitch and [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]]’ RBI single.

[[cb-san-diego-carter-rustad|Carter Rustad]] earned the win with 2.1 scoreless innings, while [[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] threw three scoreless innings and [[cb-san-diego-kieran-shaw|Kieran Shaw]] recorded the save.
[[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] went 2-for-4 with a triple, two runs and three RBIs as San Diego rallied from an early three-run deficit to defeat Vanguard 10–4 at Fowler Park.

San Diego answered Vanguard’s first-inning three-spot with five runs in the second. Luevano’s two-run single tied the game, then [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] reached on an error for the lead. Luevano later tripled home a run in the fifth before [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] added a sacrifice fly.

[[cb-san-diego-lucas-braun|Lucas Braun]] earned the win with three scoreless innings and three strikeouts after entering in the second. [[cb-san-diego-cole-colleran|Cole Colleran]] followed with 2.1 scoreless innings and five strikeouts.
[[cb-cal-state-fullerton-tanner-bibee|Tanner Bibee]] carried Cal State Fullerton to a 3–1 win over San Diego at Goodwin Field, allowing one run on four hits across seven innings.

Fullerton took a first-inning lead on an RBI sacrifice fly, but [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]] tied it with a seventh-inning RBI single after [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] doubled and [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] reached on a hit.

The Titans answered in the eighth with a two-run triple. San Diego received 3.2 scoreless innings and four strikeouts from [[cb-san-diego-carter-rustad|Carter Rustad]], but [[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] was charged with the loss.
[[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] went 3-for-4 with two doubles, a home run and three RBIs as San Diego defeated Cal State Fullerton 8–2 at Fowler Park.

Luevano tied the game with an RBI double in the fourth, homered in the sixth, and capped San Diego’s five-run seventh with another RBI double. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] went 2-for-4 with an RBI, while [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] had two hits and drove in a run.

[[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] earned the win with seven innings of one-run ball, striking out seven. [[cb-san-diego-kieran-shaw|Kieran Shaw]] closed with two innings and three strikeouts.
[[cb-san-francisco-luke-keaschall|Luke Keaschall]] went 5-for-6 with three runs and three RBIs as San Francisco routed San Diego 12–1 at Fowler Park.

The Dons scored in each of the first five innings, including a four-run second. Keaschall collected RBI singles in the second, fifth and seventh, while [[cb-san-francisco-darius-foster|Darius Foster]] added three hits and two RBIs.

[[cb-san-francisco-landen-bourassa|Landen Bourassa]] earned the win by holding San Diego to one run over eight innings. [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]] drove in the Toreros’ lone run with a fifth-inning single.
[[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] drove in three runs as San Diego defeated San Francisco 7–5 at Fowler Park.

San Diego jumped ahead with four runs in the first, highlighted by [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]]’s two-run double and [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]]’ RBI single. Sim added a two-run single in the third, then supplied an eighth-inning sacrifice fly for insurance.

[[cb-san-diego-jake-miller|Jake Miller]] earned the win after allowing two earned runs over five innings. [[cb-san-diego-kieran-shaw|Kieran Shaw]] struck out three across two scoreless innings for the save.
[[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] homered, drove in two and scored twice as San Diego beat San Francisco 8–1 to close the Fowler Park series.

San Diego took an early lead on [[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]]’s RBI double, then broke the 1–1 tie in the fifth on sacrifice flies by Worthington and [[cb-san-diego-paul-kunst|Paul Kunst]]. Worthington’s seventh-inning homer made it 4–1 before the Toreros added four in the eighth.

[[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] earned the win with five innings of one-run ball. [[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] worked two scoreless innings, and [[cb-san-diego-jack-hyde|Jack Hyde]] finished the game for his first save.
[[cb-cal-state-bakersfield-aaron-charles|Aaron Charles]] threw five scoreless innings as CSU Bakersfield held off UC San Diego 3–2 at Triton Ballpark.

The Roadrunners scored all three runs in the fourth, with [[cb-cal-state-bakersfield-jacen-roberson|Jacen Roberson]] driving in the first run and [[cb-cal-state-bakersfield-nick-grossman|Nick Grossman]] adding an RBI single. UC San Diego rallied in the seventh when [[cb-uc-san-diego-blake-baumgartner|Blake Baumgartner]] doubled home two.

UC San Diego collected nine hits but stranded nine runners. [[cb-uc-san-diego-chris-gilmartin|Chris Gilmartin]] supplied three scoreless relief innings, while Bakersfield’s bullpen protected Charles’s lead for the save.
[[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] went 2-for-4 with two runs and two RBIs as San Diego beat Pepperdine 8–3 at Fowler Park.

The Toreros opened with a first-inning run on [[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]]’s RBI single, added two in the fourth, and broke the game open with five in the sixth. [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] drove in three runs, while [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]] added a hit and an RBI.

[[cb-san-diego-jake-miller|Jake Miller]] earned the win, and San Diego’s bullpen held Pepperdine to three runs despite 10 hits. [[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]], [[cb-san-diego-jack-hyde|Jack Hyde]] and [[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] covered the final three innings.
[[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] went 2-for-4 with a double, two runs and two RBIs as San Diego held off Pepperdine 7–6 at Fowler Park.

Pepperdine scored in the first, but San Diego answered with five in the bottom half. Luevano’s two-run double put the Toreros ahead, then [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] singled in another run and [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] drove in two on sacrifice flies.

[[cb-san-diego-carter-rustad|Carter Rustad]] earned the win with four scoreless innings of relief, striking out four. [[cb-san-diego-kieran-shaw|Kieran Shaw]] weathered a two-hit ninth to secure the save.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] delivered a three-run double in the bottom of the ninth as San Diego stormed back to beat Pepperdine 10–9 at Fowler Park.

The Toreros trailed 9–5 entering the ninth. [[cb-san-diego-tora-otsuka|Tora Otsuka]] and [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] scored ahead of Ricketts’ tying three-run double, then [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] singled in the tying run and [[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] was hit by a pitch with the bases loaded for the walk-off.
[[cb-san-diego-lucas-braun|Lucas Braun]] earned the win with 2.2 scoreless relief innings and three strikeouts after San Diego’s bullpen held Pepperdine scoreless across the final four innings.
[[cb-byu-andrew-pintar|Andrew Pintar]] went 3-for-5 with two home runs, a triple, three runs and four RBIs as BYU outlasted San Diego 6–4 in 10 innings at Fowler Park.

Pintar homered in the first, tripled in two runs during BYU’s third-inning rally, then tied the game with a two-run homer in the 10th. San Diego had drawn even on [[cb-san-diego-adam-lopez|Adam Lopez]]’s solo homer and took a 4–3 lead in the seventh when [[cb-san-diego-thomas-luevano|Thomas Luevano]] doubled home [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]].

[[cb-san-diego-jake-miller|Jake Miller]] struck out 14 over seven innings, allowing two earned runs. [[cb-byu-reid-mclaughlin|Reid McLaughlin]] worked the final two innings for the win after [[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] took the loss in extra innings.
[[cb-byu-mitch-mcintyre|Mitch McIntyre]] went 3-for-5 with a double, a run and three RBIs as BYU held off San Diego 11–10 at Fowler Park.

BYU broke the game open with seven runs in the second, with [[cb-byu-mitch-mcintyre|McIntyre]]’s two-run double supplying the first runs before [[cb-byu-andrew-pintar|Andrew Pintar]] and [[cb-byu-brock-watkins|Brock Watkins]] added RBI singles. Pintar finished 3-for-6 with two RBIs in the win.

San Diego rallied from an 11–6 ninth-inning deficit, getting a two-run homer from [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] and late RBIs from [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] and [[cb-san-diego-adam-lopez|Adam Lopez]], but [[cb-byu-carter-smith|Carter Smith]] recorded the final three outs for his first save.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 3-for-5 with a double, three runs and an RBI as San Diego erased a three-run ninth-inning deficit to walk off BYU, 13–12, at Fowler Park.

The Toreros built a 7–0 lead in the third, with [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Ricketts]]’ RBI single and [[cb-san-diego-camden-vasquez|Camden Vasquez]]’s two-run performance helping fuel the inning, but BYU answered with eight runs in the fourth. [[cb-byu-cole-gambill|Cole Gambill]] went 3-for-6 with a homer and four RBIs for the Cougars.

After BYU carried a 12–9 lead into the ninth, [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] singled home Ricketts, [[cb-san-diego-max-jung-goldberg|Max Jung-Goldberg]] walked in a run, and sacrifice flies by [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] and [[cb-san-diego-shane-mcguire|Shane McGuire]] completed the comeback. [[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] earned the win with two scoreless relief innings.
[[cb-san-diego-garrett-rennie|Garrett Rennie]] allowed one unearned run over 6.1 innings as San Diego opened its season with an 11–1 win over Oregon at Fowler Park.

[[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] gave the Toreros an immediate lead with a two-run first-inning homer, while [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] finished 2-for-4 with two runs and two RBIs. Rennie scattered six hits, walked two and struck out five.

San Diego turned a 4–1 game into a rout with seven runs in the seventh. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] delivered a two-run single, [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] singled in two more, and [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] and Jefferis added RBI hits.
[[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] struck out 12 over 5.2 innings as San Diego beat Oregon 10–4 to start the season 2–0 at Fowler Park.

The Toreros scored seven times in the third, highlighted by [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]]’s three-run triple. [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] went 2-for-3 with two runs and an RBI, and [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] added a sacrifice fly.

Oregon cut the margin to 9–4 through six, but [[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Mautz]] limited the Ducks to three earned runs before [[cb-san-diego-jack-hyde|Jack Hyde]] closed with 3.1 scoreless innings and three strikeouts for his first save.
[[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] went 3-for-4 with two RBIs as San Diego edged Oregon 5–4 at Fowler Park to complete a three-game sweep.

After Oregon opened the scoring, [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Costello]] put San Diego ahead with a two-run single in the third. The Toreros added fourth-inning RBIs from [[cb-san-diego-camden-vasquez|Camden Vasquez]] and [[cb-san-diego-ariel-armas|Ariel Armas]], but Oregon tied it on homers by [[cb-oregon-gavin-grant|Gavin Grant]] and [[cb-oregon-brennan-milone|Brennan Milone]] plus an eighth-inning RBI double.

In the bottom of the eighth, Armas drew a bases-loaded walk to score [[cb-san-diego-casey-cummings|Casey Cummings]] with the go-ahead run. [[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] earned the win with 1.2 innings and three strikeouts, and [[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] worked a scoreless ninth for the save.
[[cb-san-diego-camden-vasquez|Camden Vasquez]] went 4-for-4 with a home run, four RBIs and a run scored, but Oregon rallied past San Diego 21–11 in an eight-inning game at Fowler Park.

Vasquez drove in the first run with a second-inning single, hit a two-run homer in the fourth, and added a sacrifice fly in the sixth. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] went 3-for-4 with three runs, while [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] collected three hits, two runs and an RBI.

San Diego led 11–9 heading into the eighth, but Oregon scored 12 times in the inning before the game ended because of a curfew. [[cb-oregon-josiah-cromwick|Josiah Cromwick]] hit a grand slam in the outburst and finished with five RBIs, while [[cb-oregon-drew-cowley|Drew Cowley]] went 3-for-4 with four RBIs.
[[cb-unlv-josh-ibarra|Josh Ibarra]] threw five scoreless innings, allowing two hits, as UNLV beat San Diego 2–1 at Fowler Park.

The game remained scoreless until [[cb-unlv-diego-alarcon|Diego Alarcon]] led off the sixth with a homer. Alarcon went 2-for-5 with both UNLV runs, then scored an unearned run in the eighth on [[cb-unlv-henry-zeisler|Henry Zeisler]]’s sacrifice fly.

[[cb-san-diego-garrett-rennie|Garrett Rennie]] kept San Diego in it with seven innings of one-run ball and six strikeouts. The Toreros rallied in the ninth when [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] singled home [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]], but [[cb-unlv-nick-rupp|Nick Rupp]] finished a four-inning save.
[[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] threw six scoreless innings with nine strikeouts as San Diego blanked Fresno State 4–0 at Fowler Park.

Mautz limited the Bulldogs to three hits and two walks, while [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] opened the scoring with a second-inning homer. [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] added an RBI single in the fifth and [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] drove in another run in the seventh.

[[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] capped the scoring with a solo homer in the eighth. [[cb-san-diego-jack-hyde|Jack Hyde]] followed Mautz with two scoreless innings for his second save, completing San Diego’s 12-strikeout shutout.
[[cb-unlv-eric-bigani|Eric Bigani]] went 2-for-5 with a homer and five RBIs as UNLV beat San Diego 16–9 at Fowler Park.

UNLV scored eight runs in the second, capped by [[cb-unlv-austin-kryszczuk|Austin Kryszczuk]]’s three-run triple, then added three more in the fourth on [[cb-unlv-henry-zeisler|Henry Zeisler]]’s three-run homer. Bigani later hit a three-run homer in the sixth as the Rebels built a 14–2 lead.

San Diego answered with five in the sixth on [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]]’s grand slam, and Sim finished 2-for-4 with five RBIs. [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] added a home run and RBI single, while [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] went 2-for-3 with three runs.
[[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] went 5-for-5 with two home runs, a double, two runs and seven RBIs as San Diego walked off Dallas Baptist 9–8 at Fowler Park.

Sim hit a two-run homer in the second, followed [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]]’ two-run sixth-inning homer with another two-run blast in the eighth, and came to the plate again with San Diego trailing by one in the ninth. [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] reached base three times and scored all three times.

After Dallas Baptist retook the lead in the ninth, Sim ripped a bases-loaded double down the left-field line to score Peraza, Ricketts and [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] for the walk-off. [[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] earned the win with a perfect ninth inning and three strikeouts.
[[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] drove in three runs with a two-run homer and a sacrifice fly, but Dallas Baptist beat San Diego 8–6 at Fowler Park.

Dallas Baptist hit six home runs, including a two-run first-inning shot by [[cb-dallas-baptist-miguel-santos|Miguel Santos]], solo homers from [[cb-dallas-baptist-jace-grady|Jace Grady]] and Cole Moore, and a two-run homer from [[cb-dallas-baptist-blayne-jones|Blayne Jones]] in the seventh. Jones finished 2-for-4 with two runs and two RBIs.

San Diego answered a 5–1 deficit with a four-run fifth: [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] hit a two-run homer and Costello followed with his two-run shot. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] added a solo homer, but Costello’s seventh-inning sacrifice fly was the final Torero run.
[[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] went 2-for-5 with a three-run homer, but Dallas Baptist held off San Diego 5–4 at Fowler Park.

Dallas Baptist built a 5–0 lead behind solo homers from [[cb-dallas-baptist-nate-rombach|Nate Rombach]] and [[cb-dallas-baptist-blayne-jones|Blayne Jones]], then a three-run seventh fueled by [[cb-dallas-baptist-andrew-benefield|Andrew Benefield]]’s two-run double. [[cb-dallas-baptist-alec-baker|Alec Baker]] earned the win with 1.1 scoreless innings and three strikeouts.

[[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Meidroth]]’s seventh-inning homer brought San Diego within two, and [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] singled home [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] in the eighth. [[cb-dallas-baptist-kyle-rich|Kyle Rich]] then stranded the tying run in scoring position to secure the save.
[[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] struck out seven in three perfect innings to save San Diego’s 2–0 win over UC San Diego at Fowler Park.

The Toreros scored both runs in the fourth despite managing only three hits. [[cb-san-diego-ariel-armas|Ariel Armas]] grounded in the first run, then [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] scored on a wild pitch after [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] walked.

[[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] earned the win with 4.1 scoreless innings and five strikeouts, while [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 2-for-3 with a triple. The Torero staff held UC San Diego to four hits and struck out 14.

paragraphs: [[cb-grand-canyon-tayler-aguilar|Tayler Aguilar]] went 2-for-4 with a homer, two runs and three RBIs as Grand Canyon rallied past San Diego 6–5 at GCU Ballpark.

San Diego erased Grand Canyon’s early 3–0 lead and went ahead 5–3, paced by [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]]’s 3-for-4 night with a homer and a double. [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] tied the game in the third with a two-run double.

Aguilar’s two-run homer tied the score in the eighth, then [[cb-grand-canyon-elijah-buries|Elijah Buries]] doubled home the winning run in the ninth. [[cb-grand-canyon-eli-ankeney|Eli Ankeney]] earned the win with two scoreless innings and three strikeouts.
[[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] allowed three hits over seven scoreless innings and struck out nine as San Diego beat Grand Canyon 7–1 at GCU Ballpark.

[[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] went 3-for-4 with two runs and two RBIs, starting a three-run second with an RBI single before [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] singled in two. [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] added a fourth-inning solo homer.

[[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] doubled home a run in the seventh, and [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|DeCriscio]] added another RBI single in the eighth as the Toreros finished with 15 hits and 12 strikeouts.
[[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] went 3-for-4 with two RBIs as San Diego came from behind to beat Grand Canyon 7–5 at GCU Ballpark.

San Diego trailed 3–1 in the seventh before [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Allen]] singled in a run and [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] tied the game with a groundout. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] and [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] then hit back-to-back solo homers in the eighth.

[[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Allen]] added an RBI single in the eighth, and [[cb-san-diego-jack-hyde|Jack Hyde]] stranded the tying run in the ninth for his third save after [[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] earned the win.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 3-for-5 with a home run, two runs and three RBIs as San Diego held off Cal State Fullerton 11–10 at Fowler Park.

After the Titans tied the game in the seventh, [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Ricketts]] put the Toreros ahead for good with an RBI double. [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] followed with a two-run double, and [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] added a bunt single that made it 8–4.

[[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] capped the six-run seventh with a two-run single before Ricketts supplied an eighth-inning solo homer. [[cb-san-diego-cole-colleran|Cole Colleran]] earned the save by retiring the final out with the tying run on base.
[[cb-pepperdine-brandon-llewellyn|Brandon Llewellyn]] threw eight scoreless innings as Pepperdine beat San Diego 3–0 at Eddy D. Field Stadium.

[[cb-pepperdine-ryan-johnson|Ryan Johnson]] broke a scoreless game in the second with a two-run double, scoring Mike Malinchak and [[cb-pepperdine-devon-walczykowski|Devon Walczykowski]]. Walczykowski then added an eighth-inning solo homer.

Llewellyn scattered six hits, walked three and struck out four before Grant Georges recorded the final three outs for his fifth save. [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] had two of San Diego’s six hits, while [[cb-san-diego-garrett-rennie|Garrett Rennie]] allowed two runs in five innings.
[[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] struck out eight over six innings as San Diego beat Pepperdine 8–1 at Eddy D. Field Stadium.

[[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] led off with a home run, while [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] drove in a run with a second-inning bunt single and [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] added a fifth-inning RBI single.

San Diego broke the game open with five runs in the ninth, aided by two wild pitches before [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Meidroth]] singled home a run and [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] delivered a two-run single. [[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] followed Mautz with two scoreless innings and four strikeouts.
[[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] went 3-for-4 with a double, a home run, two runs and three RBIs as San Diego completed the series with a 6–3 win at Pepperdine.

The Toreros scored all five of their early runs in the third. [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Meidroth]] doubled in two, [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] followed with an RBI single, and [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] hit a two-run homer.

[[cb-san-diego-ian-churchill|Ian Churchill]] earned the win with six strikeouts in 3.2 innings of relief, then [[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] recorded the final out for his second save. Meidroth’s ninth-inning homer supplied the insurance run.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 3-for-3 with a double, two runs and a walk as San Diego beat UC Irvine 6–5 in 10 innings at Fowler Park.
[[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] gave the Toreros a 5–2 lead with a three-run homer in the seventh, but UC Irvine tied the game on Justin Torres’ three-run homer in the ninth.

In the 10th, Ricketts scored the winning run when [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] reached on a fielder’s choice. [[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] earned the win after striking out eight over the final three innings.
[[cb-san-diego-rj-teijeiro|RJ Teijeiro]] ended a 10-inning battle with a two-run walk-off homer as San Diego beat Saint Mary’s 4–2 at Fowler Park.

Teijeiro also drove in San Diego’s fourth-inning run with a single, finishing 2-for-4 with three RBIs. [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 3-for-4 with a double and triple, while [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] added three hits.

[[cb-san-diego-garrett-rennie|Garrett Rennie]] limited Saint Mary’s to one run over 7.1 innings with eight strikeouts. [[cb-san-diego-ian-churchill|Ian Churchill]] struck out all three batters in the 10th before Teijeiro’s walk-off.
[[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] allowed one run over 6.2 innings and struck out seven as San Diego beat Saint Mary’s 4–1 at Fowler Park.

[[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] put San Diego ahead with a second-inning RBI single, and [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] added a sacrifice fly in the fourth. Saint Mary’s cut the deficit to one on Dalton Mashore’s solo homer in the fifth.

[[cb-san-diego-camden-vasquez|Camden Vasquez]] supplied the breathing room in the eighth with a two-run double, scoring [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] and Jack Costello. [[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] struck out four over 2.1 scoreless innings for the save.
[[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] went 2-for-3 with two runs, two RBIs and two walks as San Diego rallied past Saint Mary’s 11–6 at Fowler Park.

The Toreros erased an early 3–0 deficit with three runs in the second, then matched Saint Mary’s three-run fifth. [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] reached on a throwing error that brought in a run, [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] tied it with a sacrifice fly, and [[cb-san-diego-camden-vasquez|Camden Vasquez]] followed with an RBI single.

San Diego broke the tie with five eighth-inning runs. [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Worthington]] singled in two, and [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] followed with a two-run homer. [[cb-san-diego-james-sashin|James Sashin]] earned his first win.
[[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] earned the win with 2.2 scoreless relief innings and three strikeouts as San Diego beat Cal Baptist 7–2 at Totman Stadium.

San Diego built a six-run lead through two innings. [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] doubled in a run, [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] followed with an RBI single, and [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] added another RBI single in the five-run second.

Cal Baptist answered with back-to-back homers in the bottom of the second, but the Torero bullpen held it there. [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] added an eighth-inning RBI single for the final margin.
[[cb-san-diego-ian-churchill|Ian Churchill]] struck out seven of the eight batters he faced over 2.2 perfect innings as San Diego beat San Francisco 8–3 at Benedetti Diamond.

The Toreros struck for five runs in the second. [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] opened the scoring with an RBI single, then [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] drove in two with a double and [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] added an RBI single.

Ricketts later singled in two more runs in the fourth, giving him three RBIs. [[cb-san-diego-garrett-rennie|Garrett Rennie]] earned the win, while Churchill closed the final 2.2 innings without allowing a baserunner.
[[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] struck out nine in five innings, but San Diego fell to San Francisco 6–5 at Benedetti Diamond.

San Diego built a 5–0 lead through three innings. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] drove in the first run, and [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]], [[cb-san-diego-ariel-armas|Ariel Armas]], [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] and [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] each added an RBI during a four-run third.

After [[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Mautz]] left, the Dons rallied with homers in the third, fifth and eighth. Darius Foster’s solo homer in the eighth put San Francisco ahead, and Josh Mollerus closed it for the save.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 3-for-4 and scored a run, but San Diego was edged 3–2 by San Francisco on a ninth-inning walk-off homer at Benedetti Diamond.

[[cb-san-diego-max-jung-goldberg|Max Jung-Goldberg]] scored on a wild pitch in the second, and [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] added an RBI single for a 2–0 San Diego lead. San Francisco trimmed it to one with a third-inning RBI single.

[[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] kept the Dons off the board over 2.2 innings while striking out five, but Zach Freeman’s two-run homer in the ninth ended it. [[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] took the loss.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 4-for-5 with a double, a home run and four RBIs as San Diego routed UC San Diego 13–4 at Triton Ballpark.

San Diego broke the game open with six runs in the second. [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] walked in a run, [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] singled home another, and [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] drove in two with a single before Ricketts doubled in the sixth run.
[[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Sim]] finished 3-for-4 with five runs, three RBIs and a sixth-inning homer. Ricketts added a two-run homer in the fourth as San Diego piled up 13 runs and 13 hits.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 2-for-4 and accounted for both San Diego runs with a two-run homer, but the Toreros fell 6–2 at Portland.

Ricketts’ sixth-inning homer scored [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] and cut Portland’s lead to 5–2. It was San Diego’s only extra-base hit and one of just three hits against Pilots starter Brett Gillis.

Portland built its lead with a three-run third and two more in the fifth, led by Trace Tammaro’s three RBIs. [[cb-san-diego-gabe-maya|Gabe Maya]] struck out five over three innings of relief, allowing an unearned run.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 2-for-5 with a home run, two runs and three RBIs as San Diego rallied past Portland 8–6 in the first game of a doubleheader at Joe Etzel Field.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Ricketts]] gave the Toreros a 5–1 lead with a two-run homer in the fifth, but Portland scored five times in the sixth to move ahead 6–5.

San Diego answered with three in the seventh. Ricketts tied it with an RBI single, and [[cb-san-diego-rj-teijeiro|RJ Teijeiro]] singled home two more runs for the lead. [[cb-san-diego-ian-churchill|Ian Churchill]] worked 2.1 scoreless innings for his first save.
[[cb-san-diego-rj-teijeiro|RJ Teijeiro]] went 4-for-5 with two doubles, a triple, a run and an RBI, but San Diego fell to Portland 5–4 in 10 innings in the second game of the doubleheader.

San Diego rallied from a 3–0 deficit with [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]]' seventh-inning RBI double, [[cb-san-diego-max-jung-goldberg|Max Jung-Goldberg]]'s RBI single and Teijeiro’s eighth-inning RBI single. [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] tied the game in the ninth when he reached on an error.

Portland matched the ninth-inning run with a bases-loaded walk, then won in the 10th when Tony Boetto reached on an error and an unearned run scored. [[cb-san-diego-james-sashin|James Sashin]] threw 2.2 scoreless innings before the late finish.
[[cb-san-diego-jack-hyde|Jack Hyde]] threw two scoreless innings with two strikeouts to earn the win as San Diego beat San Diego State 8–3 at Fowler Park.
The Toreros fell behind 3–2 in the third, then [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]]'s sacrifice fly tied the game in the fifth before a four-run sixth opened the game.

[[cb-san-diego-camden-vasquez|Camden Vasquez]] walked with the bases loaded to put San Diego ahead, and [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] reached on an error that scored two more. Meidroth later added a sacrifice fly, while Hyde, [[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] and Cole Colleran held the Aztecs scoreless over the final four innings.
[[cb-san-diego-ian-churchill|Ian Churchill]] threw six scoreless relief innings as San Diego completed a 9–8, 14-inning comeback win over Loyola Marymount at Fowler Park.

The Toreros trailed 7–1 after four innings before [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] drove in a run, [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] doubled home two, and [[cb-san-diego-rj-teijeiro|RJ Teijeiro]] singled home another in a six-run fourth.

LMU pushed its lead back to 8–7, but Teijeiro’s ninth-inning RBI single tied it. Churchill kept the Lions off the board from the eighth through the 13th, and Allen singled home [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] in the 14th for the walk-off.
[[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] threw a six-hit shutout with eight strikeouts as San Diego edged Loyola Marymount 1–0 at Fowler Park.

Mautz stranded a pair of Lions in scoring position in the third and held LMU scoreless through nine innings, while [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] supplied two of San Diego’s four hits.
Ricketts opened the ninth with a double and scored the winning run when [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] singled to right with one out.

paragraphs: [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] drove in San Diego’s only run with a first-inning RBI double, but Loyola Marymount pulled away for an 8–1 win at Fowler Park.
After [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] scored on Ricketts’ double, the Lions tied it on a sacrifice fly in the second and went ahead on Diego Baqueiro’s RBI double in the third.

San Diego had eight hits, including two by [[cb-san-diego-rj-teijeiro|RJ Teijeiro]], but left 10 runners on base. LMU broke the game open with two runs in the eighth and Grant Weiss’ four-run homer in the ninth.
[[cb-san-diego-rj-teijeiro|RJ Teijeiro]] went 3-for-6 with a two-run homer, two runs and two RBIs as San Diego routed San Diego State 15–1 at Tony Gwynn Stadium.
The Toreros broke open the game with eight runs in the second, including [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]]’s two-run double. San Diego State committed five errors in the loss.

Teijeiro’s homer capped a four-run third, and [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] added three RBIs on a single and two sacrifice flies. [[cb-san-diego-ryan-kysar|Ryan Kysar]] earned the win with five innings of one-run ball.
[[cb-stanford-carter-graham|Carter Graham]] went 2-for-5 with a double, a home run and four RBIs as Stanford defeated Grand Canyon 11–1 at Tony Gwynn Stadium.
[[cb-grand-canyon-cade-verdusco|Cade Verdusco]] put Grand Canyon ahead in the second, but Stanford answered with four runs in the inning and never trailed again.

Graham’s two-run double keyed the second-inning response, then [[cb-stanford-braden-montgomery|Braden Montgomery]] hit two solo homers and Graham added a two-run blast in the sixth. [[cb-stanford-alex-williams|Alex Williams]] allowed one run over eight innings for the win.
[[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] went 2-for-3 with a double and three RBIs, but San Diego’s early lead slipped away in an 8–7 loss at Cal State Fullerton.

San Diego scored five times in the second and added two on Allen’s third-inning double for a 7–3 lead. [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] drove in two runs during the second-inning outburst.
Fullerton rallied with two runs in the fifth, two in the seventh and the go-ahead run in the eighth. [[cb-cal-state-fullerton-caden-connor|Caden Connor]] went 3-for-5 with three RBIs for the Titans.
[[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] went 2-for-5 with a two-run homer as San Diego beat Santa Clara 8–3 at Fowler Park.

After Santa Clara scored in the first, [[cb-san-diego-rj-teijeiro|RJ Teijeiro]] tied the game with a groundout before Meidroth’s two-run homer and [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]]’s solo shot put the Toreros ahead.

[[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] added a third-inning homer, and [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] tripled home two in the fifth. Ryan Kysar earned the win and Ian Churchill recorded the save.
[[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] went 3-for-5 with two home runs, four runs and seven RBIs as San Diego overwhelmed Santa Clara 17–4 at Fowler Park.
San Diego scored eight times in the first and four more in the second, highlighted by Meidroth’s grand slam. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] added a triple, three hits and four RBIs.
Meidroth hit his second homer in the fourth, while [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 3-for-4 with a homer and three RBIs. [[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] earned the win.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 3-for-4 with an RBI, but San Diego fell to Santa Clara 3–2 at Fowler Park.
Santa Clara scored in the first, fourth and sixth while San Diego countered with [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]]’s RBI single in the second and Ricketts’ eighth-inning RBI single.

[[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] threw two scoreless innings with three strikeouts, and [[cb-san-diego-garrett-rennie|Garrett Rennie]] allowed one unearned run over four innings in relief.
[[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] provided San Diego’s only offense with a seventh-inning homer, but UC Irvine won 6–1 at Anteater Ballpark.
UC Irvine scored twice in the first and added three in the fourth to build its lead. [[cb-uc-irvine-ben-fitzgerald|Ben Fitzgerald]] went 2-for-4 with two RBIs.
[[cb-san-diego-jack-hyde|Jack Hyde]] threw three scoreless innings in relief, but David Vizcaino held San Diego to two hits over seven innings.
[[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] went 3-for-4 with a homer, two runs and an RBI as San Diego defeated Pacific 9–4.
[[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] tripled home two in a four-run third, and [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] finished with two hits and two RBIs.
Meidroth homered in the sixth, and [[cb-san-diego-ryan-kysar|Ryan Kysar]] earned the win with seven innings and seven strikeouts.
[[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] hit a three-run homer in the eighth as San Diego rallied past Pacific 9–6.
Pacific took a 6–5 lead on a three-run seventh-inning homer, but [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] homered earlier and [[cb-san-diego-rj-teijeiro|RJ Teijeiro]] drove in three runs.
[[cb-san-diego-ian-churchill|Ian Churchill]] earned the win with 4.1 innings and six strikeouts, and Teijeiro added a ninth-inning RBI single.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 2-for-4 with a homer, three runs and three RBIs as San Diego completed a 12–5 win over Pacific.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Ricketts’]] two-run first-inning homer gave San Diego an early lead, and he added an RBI single during a four-run fifth that put the Toreros ahead for good.
[[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] went 3-for-5 with a triple and three RBIs, while [[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] threw 5.1 scoreless innings with seven strikeouts for the win.
[[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] went 4-for-5 with a double, a homer and four RBIs as San Diego beat Cal Baptist 9–2 at Fowler Park.
Costello’s two-run double and [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]]’ RBI double helped San Diego take a three-run first-inning lead, and Jefferis added another RBI in the third.

After Cal Baptist cut it to 5–2 on a two-run seventh-inning homer, [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] singled in a run and Costello answered with a two-run homer. [[cb-san-diego-james-sashin|James Sashin]] earned the win with two scoreless innings.
[[cb-gonzaga-gabriel-hughes|Gabriel Hughes]] struck out nine over 8.2 innings as No. 10 Gonzaga defeated San Diego 8–4 at Fowler Park.
San Diego took a 2–1 lead in the third on [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]]’s two-run triple, but Gonzaga tied it on a fifth-inning homer and scored four times in the sixth.

[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] homered in the sixth and [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] added a sacrifice fly to trim the margin to 6–4, before Gonzaga added two ninth-inning insurance runs. [[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] struck out eight in 5.1 innings in the loss.

paragraphs: [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] went 2-for-3 with a walk, a run and two RBIs as San Diego answered an early deficit to beat No. 10 Gonzaga 7–4.

Gonzaga scored twice in the second, but Allen’s two-run single began a six-run San Diego answer. [[cb-san-diego-chase-meidroth|Chase Meidroth]] walked in a run, [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] drove in another, and [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] singled home two.

[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] added an RBI single in the fourth, while [[cb-san-diego-ryan-kysar|Ryan Kysar]] earned the win with six innings of two-run ball. [[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] struck out two for the save.
[[cb-gonzaga-will-kempner|Will Kempner]] threw five one-hit innings with eight strikeouts as Gonzaga edged San Diego 1–0 in the second game of the doubleheader.

The only run scored in the third, when [[cb-gonzaga-cade-mcgee|Cade McGee]] singled home Tyler Rando after Rando’s double. [[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] held Gonzaga to one run over four innings in the loss.

San Diego had only two hits and struck out 13 times. [[cb-san-diego-garrett-rennie|Garrett Rennie]] supplied three scoreless innings of relief, while Michael Spellacy closed the ninth for Gonzaga’s save.

paragraphs: [[cb-uc-san-diego-noah-conlon|Noah Conlon]] held Hawai‘i to one unearned run on one hit over six innings, but UC San Diego fell 4–0 at Triton Ballpark.
Hawai‘i broke the scoreless game in the sixth on [[cb-hawaii-aaron-ujimori|Aaron Ujimori]]’s RBI groundout, then [[cb-hawaii-kyson-donahue|Kyson Donahue]] hit a solo homer in the eighth.

[[cb-hawaii-stone-miyao|Stone Miyao]] drove in two insurance runs with a ninth-inning double. UC San Diego collected five hits, but [[cb-hawaii-connor-harrison|Connor Harrison]] earned the win with 2.2 scoreless innings and [[cb-hawaii-dalton-renne|Dalton Renne]] closed for the save.

player_of_game.name: Noah Conlon
