paragraphs: [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 3-for-5 with two homers, two runs and two RBIs as San Diego rallied past San Francisco 10–5 in the WCC Tournament.
Ricketts homered in the first, but San Francisco took a 5–2 lead on three homers through the fifth. [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] then tied it with a three-run homer in the sixth.

Ricketts’ second homer put San Diego ahead in the seventh, and [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] followed with an RBI bunt before adding a two-RBI single in the eighth. [[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] earned the win with 2.2 scoreless innings and five strikeouts.
[[cb-gonzaga-enzo-apodaca|Enzo Apodaca]] went 3-for-5 with a three-run homer, a double, two runs and four RBIs as Gonzaga routed Loyola Marymount 16–2 in the WCC Tournament.

Apodaca’s three-run blast highlighted Gonzaga’s three-run second, then [[cb-gonzaga-shea-kramer|Shea Kramer]] hit a two-run homer in the third and [[cb-gonzaga-cade-mcgee|Cade McGee]] added a solo shot in the fifth.

Gonzaga broke it open with eight runs in the seventh, punctuated by [[cb-gonzaga-enzo-apodaca|Apodaca’s]] RBI double and a two-run homer by Savier Pinales. [[cb-gonzaga-owen-wild|Owen Wild]] earned the win.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 2-for-4 with a homer and four RBIs as San Diego overwhelmed Portland 22–8 in the WCC Tournament.
San Diego scored six times in the second, capped by Ricketts’ two-run homer. [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] later doubled in two more during the third as the Toreros built a 9–0 lead.

Portland cut the margin to six in the sixth, but San Diego answered with seven in the seventh. [[cb-san-diego-rj-teijeiro|RJ Teijeiro]] homered and drove in four, while [[cb-san-diego-gabe-maya|Gabe Maya]] earned the win with two scoreless relief innings.
[[cb-portland-evan-scavotto|Evan Scavotto]] went 2-for-5 with two home runs and five RBIs as Portland eliminated Loyola Marymount 10–2 in the WCC Tournament.

Loyola Marymount led 2–1 after two innings, but Portland moved ahead in the third and exploded for five in the fourth. Scavotto’s three-run homer put the Pilots in control before [[cb-portland-christian-cooney|Christian Cooney]] added a solo shot.
Scavotto struck again with a two-run homer in the ninth. [[cb-portland-eli-morse|Eli Morse]] earned the win in relief as Portland advanced with 13 hits.
[[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] went 2-for-3 with two home runs and four RBIs as San Diego rallied past No. 10 Gonzaga 5–3 in the WCC Tournament.

Gonzaga built a 3–0 lead on a first-inning Shea Kramer RBI double and third-inning home runs by Savier Pinales and Cade McGee. [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Ricketts]] erased it with a three-run homer in the fourth.

[[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] supplied the go-ahead sacrifice fly in the fifth, then Ricketts added a solo homer in the eighth. [[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] struck out nine over five innings, and [[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] saved it with two scoreless frames.
[[cb-gonzaga-will-kempner|Will Kempner]] struck out 14 over 5⅔ scoreless innings as Gonzaga blanked Portland 7–0 in the WCC Tournament.

Gonzaga manufactured its first three runs behind an RBI double from [[cb-gonzaga-enzo-apodaca|Enzo Apodaca]]’s lineup mate Tyler Rando, a solo homer and a sacrifice fly after [[cb-gonzaga-shea-kramer|Shea Kramer]] doubled and moved to third.
The Bulldogs broke it open with four ninth-inning runs, while [[cb-gonzaga-will-kempner|Kempner]], Jacob Rutherford and Michael Spellacy combined for a six-hit shutout and 17 strikeouts.
[[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] hit a go-ahead solo home run in the 11th and San Diego outlasted Gonzaga 15–12 in a WCC Tournament classic.

After Gonzaga built a 10–6 lead through seven, [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] and the Toreros erupted for six runs in the eighth to take a 12–10 lead. Gonzaga answered with a homer in the eighth and a tying RBI single in the ninth to force extras.

Costello’s 11th-inning homer put San Diego back in front, then [[cb-san-diego-cody-jefferis|Cody Jefferis]] supplied a two-run shot. [[cb-san-diego-kyle-carr|Kyle Carr]] worked two scoreless innings with three strikeouts for the win.
[[cb-san-diego-brycen-mautz|Brycen Mautz]] carried San Diego past Vanderbilt 3–2 in the Corvallis Regional, allowing one run over seven innings for his 10th win.

The Toreros took advantage of two first-inning Vanderbilt errors, then [[cb-san-diego-caleb-ricketts|Caleb Ricketts]] singled home a third-inning run and [[cb-san-diego-camden-vasquez|Camden Vasquez]] added an RBI groundout in the fourth.
Vanderbilt trimmed the margin on late solo homers, but [[cb-san-diego-ian-churchill|Ian Churchill]] recorded the final three outs for his fourth save after Ryan Robinson worked the eighth.
[[cb-oregon-state-ryan-brown|Ryan Brown]] struck out three over 1⅔ scoreless relief innings as Oregon State walked off New Mexico State 5–4 in 10 innings in the Corvallis Regional.

[[cb-oregon-state-cooper-hjerpe|Cooper Hjerpe]] struck out 10 across 6⅔ innings, but New Mexico State moved ahead with two seventh-inning runs before Oregon State answered immediately to take a 4–3 lead.

The Aggies tied it in the ninth, but Brown stranded the go-ahead runner at third and worked a clean 10th. [[cb-oregon-state-travis-bazzana|Travis Bazzana]] walked, stole second and scored the winning run when [[cb-oregon-state-justin-boyd|Justin Boyd]] drew a bases-loaded walk.
[[cb-vanderbilt-dominic-keegan|Dominic Keegan]] drove in four runs as Vanderbilt overwhelmed New Mexico State 21–1 in the Corvallis Regional elimination game.

Vanderbilt put the game away with five runs in the fifth, then added 12 more across the final four innings. [[cb-vanderbilt-parker-noland|Parker Noland]] went 3-for-6 with three RBIs, including two doubles, while [[cb-vanderbilt-tate-kolwyck|Tate Kolwyck]] reached base four times and scored four runs.

Keegan followed his first-inning sacrifice fly with a two-run homer in the eighth and an RBI walk in the ninth. [[cb-vanderbilt-dominic-keegan|Keegan]] finished 1-for-2 with three runs scored as Vanderbilt collected 18 hits.
[[cb-oregon-state-garret-forrester|Garret Forrester]] homered and drove in three as Oregon State routed San Diego 12–3 in the Corvallis Regional.

Oregon State stormed to four first-inning runs and led 8–0 by the third. [[cb-oregon-state-travis-bazzana|Travis Bazzana]] scored three times, stole two bases and later homered, while Forrester went 2-for-4 with a two-run homer and an RBI single.

San Diego got a triple from [[cb-san-diego-camden-vasquez|Camden Vasquez]] and a solo homer from [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]], but Oregon State’s Brock Townsend covered the final 3⅔ innings for the save.
[[cb-vanderbilt-dominic-keegan|Dominic Keegan]] went 4-for-6 with four RBIs and three runs as Vanderbilt eliminated San Diego 14–4 in the Corvallis Regional.

Vanderbilt scored three times in the first and never trailed. [[cb-vanderbilt-parker-noland|Parker Noland]] added three hits and three RBIs, while Keegan doubled home two in the eighth as the Commodores stretched the lead into double digits.

San Diego’s [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] went 2-for-4 with a home run and two RBIs, but Vanderbilt answered every Torero push. [[cb-vanderbilt-dominic-keegan|Keegan]] singled home a run in the seventh before Vanderbilt finished with three more in the ninth.
[[cb-vanderbilt-devin-futrell|Devin Futrell]] threw six scoreless innings as Vanderbilt defeated Oregon State 8–1 to advance from the Corvallis Regional.

The Commodores scored three in the second on a sequence of pressure plays, then [[cb-vanderbilt-spencer-jones|Spencer Jones]] hit a solo homer in the third. [[cb-vanderbilt-tate-kolwyck|Tate Kolwyck]] added an RBI single in the fourth before Vanderbilt scored three more in the sixth.

Futrell allowed five hits, walked two and struck out four before [[cb-vanderbilt-thomas-schultz|Thomas Schultz]] completed the three-inning save. Oregon State’s only run came on a seventh-inning error after [[cb-oregon-state-justin-boyd|Justin Boyd]] reached base.
[[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Austin Smith]] went 4-for-4 with two RBIs as San Diego opened its season with a 7–3 win over Nebraska at Fowler Park.
Smith’s two-run double gave the Toreros an early lead, and [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] broke a 2–2 tie with a solo homer in the sixth. Dustin Allen added a seventh-inning RBI single.

Nebraska closed within one in the eighth, but [[cb-san-diego-jack-gurevitch|Jack Gurevitch]] answered with a two-run double and Justin DeCriscio added an RBI single. [[cb-san-diego-mikiah-negrete|Mikiah Negrete]] earned the win and Ryan Robinson recorded the save.
[[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] homered, scored three times and drove in two as San Diego edged Nebraska 5–3 to clinch the series.
Sim’s two-run first-inning homer supplied the early margin, then [[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Austin Smith]] singled him home in the sixth. Nebraska tied it with a two-run homer in the eighth.

San Diego immediately answered in the bottom half as [[cb-san-diego-jack-gurevitch|Jack Gurevitch]] singled home the go-ahead run and Angelo Peraza scored on a wild pitch. Austin Smith then struck out three in the ninth for his first save.
[[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] went 3-for-5 with a homer, double, five RBIs and three runs as San Diego completed a 10–9 walk-off win over Nebraska.

Nebraska led 8–2 after four innings, but [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Sim]] keyed a five-run fifth with a three-run double, then Angelo Peraza singled him home. San Diego tied it with two sixth-inning runs.

After Nebraska moved back ahead in the sixth, [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] delivered the winning RBI single in the ninth to score Sim. [[cb-san-diego-drake-frize|Drake Frize]] earned the victory in relief.
[[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] hit two home runs and drove in seven as San Diego and Nebraska played to a 16–16 official seven-inning draw at Fowler Park.

Nebraska built a 4–1 lead before San Diego erupted for nine fourth-inning runs. [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Costello]] hit a grand slam in that outburst, then [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] added a two-run homer.

Nebraska reclaimed the lead with five in the fifth and five more in the seventh, but the Toreros answered with six in the bottom of the seventh. [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Costello]]’s three-run homer tied it at 16, ending the officially recorded draw.
[[cb-cal-state-northridge-jakob-simons|Jakob Simons]] went 2-for-4 with a home run as Cal State Northridge beat San Diego State 7–5 at Tony Gwynn Stadium.

CSUN raced to a 6–0 lead through two innings, with [[cb-cal-state-northridge-emanuel-dean|Emanuel Dean]] driving in two runs and Joey Kramer adding two RBIs. San Diego State fought back to within 6–4 by the third.

Simons’ sixth-inning solo homer gave the Matadors needed breathing room. [[cb-cal-state-northridge-kenji-pallares|Kenji Pallares]] earned the win and [[cb-cal-state-northridge-isaac-ontiveros|Isaac Ontiveros]] closed it for the save.
[[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] went 3-for-4 with two home runs, six RBIs and four runs as San Diego routed Hawai‘i 14–2.

Costello opened the scoring with a two-run homer in the first, then singled home a run during a three-run third. [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] went 3-for-5 with four runs scored, a double and a homer.

San Diego broke the game open with five in the sixth before [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Costello]] capped the scoring with a three-run homer in the seventh. Aídan Gonzalez earned the win as the Toreros limited Hawai‘i to two hits.
[[cb-unlv-alex-pimentel|Alex Pimentel]] went 4-for-5 with two doubles, two runs and three RBIs as UNLV beat UC Irvine 10–4 at Fowler Park. The Rebels collected 17 hits and never trailed.

UNLV struck for five in the first. [[cb-unlv-santino-panaro|Santino Panaro]] opened the scoring with an RBI single, [[cb-unlv-austin-kryszczuk|Austin Kryszczuk]] followed with another RBI hit, and Pimentel cleared the bases with a three-run double. [[cb-unlv-paul-myro|Paul Myro]] later doubled home two in the fifth.

[[cb-unlv-josh-sharman|Josh Sharman]] earned the win, and [[cb-unlv-jack-sellinger|Jack Sellinger]] closed it for the save. UC Irvine trimmed the margin with a seventh-inning rally capped by Tony Martinez’s two-run homer, but UNLV answered with two insurance runs in the ninth.
[[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] went 2-for-5 with a two-run homer and a walk-off RBI single as San Diego edged UNLV 6–5 at Fowler Park.

UNLV built a 3–0 fourth-inning lead on a wild pitch and Jason Sharman’s two-run double, but [[cb-san-diego-ariel-armas|Ariel Armas]] answered with a two-run double. Costello’s two-run homer put San Diego ahead in the fifth, and [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] doubled in another run in the sixth.

UNLV tied it in the seventh on [[cb-unlv-austin-kryszczuk|Austin Kryszczuk]]’s two-run homer. [[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] then delivered 2.1 scoreless innings with four strikeouts, and Costello singled home [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] in the ninth to finish it.
[[cb-uc-irvine-dub-gleed|Dub Gleed]] went 3-for-5 with two runs and an RBI as UC Irvine erased an early deficit and beat San Diego 14–6 at Fowler Park.

San Diego scored twice in the first and restored a 3–2 lead in the fifth, but the Anteaters broke through for six in the sixth. [[cb-uc-irvine-chase-call|Chase Call]] delivered a two-run single, while Gleed doubled and [[cb-uc-irvine-dub-gleed|Gleed]] later scored during the rally.

UC Irvine added six more in the seventh, highlighted by Tony Martinez’s three-run homer. [[cb-uc-irvine-dub-gleed|Gleed]] finished 3-for-5 as the Anteaters turned a one-run game into a rout, while Cooper Robinson earned the win with four innings of one-run relief and four strikeouts.
[[cb-oregon-jace-stoffal|Jace Stoffal]] held San Diego to one run on two hits across five innings, striking out four, as Oregon beat the Toreros 3–2 at PK Park.

San Diego struck first on [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]]’s first-inning solo homer, but Oregon moved ahead in the fourth when Drew Cowley doubled home two. [[cb-oregon-jacob-walsh|Jacob Walsh]] added a seventh-inning solo homer for the eventual winning run.

San Diego made it 3–2 in the eighth when [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] singled home a run, but [[cb-oregon-josh-mollerus|Josh Mollerus]] recorded the final four outs for the save. Stoffal earned the victory, while [[cb-san-diego-drake-frize|Drake Frize]] took the loss.

player_of_game.name: Jace Stoffal
player_of_game.line: 5.0 IP, 2 H, ER, 2 BB, 4 K, W

paragraphs: [[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Austin Smith]] went 2-for-4 with a double and two RBIs, but Oregon walked off San Diego 4–3 in the ninth inning at PK Park.

San Diego took a 2–0 lead on Will Worthington’s second-inning homer and an unearned third-inning run. Oregon answered with three in the third, including Drew Cowley’s two-run double, before Smith doubled home [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] in the seventh to tie it.

With two outs in the ninth, Tanner Smith doubled home the winning run. [[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Smith]] accounted for two of San Diego’s six hits, while Logan Mercado earned the win with 3.2 innings of relief and [[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] took the loss.
[[cb-oregon-colby-shade|Colby Shade]] went 3-for-4 with a double, a three-run homer, two runs and six RBIs as Oregon routed San Diego 13–0 at PK Park.
Oregon scored twice in the fourth, then broke it open with four in the fifth. [[cb-oregon-jacob-walsh|Jacob Walsh]] singled home a run before Shade’s three-run double made it 6–0.

The Ducks put up five more in the sixth, capped by Shade’s three-run homer, and [[cb-oregon-sabin-ceballos|Sabin Ceballos]] added a two-run homer in the seventh. Jackson Pace started the shutout, while San Diego was held to four hits.
[[cb-oregon-drew-cowley|Drew Cowley]] went 1-for-4 and broke the game open with a two-run single in the seventh as Oregon completed a 5–1 win over San Diego at PK Park.

Oregon opened the scoring on [[cb-oregon-rikuu-nishida|Rikuu Nishida]]’s first-inning homer, then added solo homers from [[cb-oregon-colby-shade|Colby Shade]] and Gavin Grant. San Diego’s lone run came in the second when Chris Esquivel hit a sacrifice fly.

Cowley’s seventh-inning single scored two for the final margin. [[cb-oregon-drew-cowley|Cowley]] supplied Oregon’s only multi-RBI hit, while Austin Anderson earned the win in relief and San Diego managed three hits.
[[cb-oregon-state-travis-bazzana|Travis Bazzana]] went 3-for-5 with a double, triple, homer, two runs and five RBIs as Oregon State beat San Diego 9–4 at Goss Stadium.

San Diego led 2–0 in the third before Bazzana doubled home a run and [[cb-oregon-state-garret-forrester|Garret Forrester]] tied it with an RBI single. Bazzana added a solo homer in the sixth after Oregon State had moved ahead.

The Beavers broke it open with three in the eighth when [[cb-oregon-state-travis-bazzana|Bazzana]] tripled home three runs. [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] drove in two of San Diego’s four runs, while Justin Thorsteinson earned the win in relief.
[[cb-san-diego-james-sashin|James Sashin]] struck out eight while allowing one run over six innings as San Diego beat Pacific 9–3 at Fowler Park.

After Pacific scored first, James Arakawa doubled in two runs in the bottom of the first. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] singled home a run in the second, and Angelo Peraza’s solo homer made it 4–1 in the third.

[[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Sim]] went 3-for-4 with a homer, three RBIs and two runs, adding an eighth-inning solo shot. San Diego scored through the first five innings, while Sashin’s start kept Pacific from mounting a response until the ninth.
[[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] went 3-for-4 with a double, a homer, three runs and two RBIs as San Diego rallied past Pacific 16–9 at Fowler Park.

Pacific built an 8–2 lead through six innings despite 19 hits, but [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] doubled home three in the sixth to cut the deficit. Sim had homered in the first and later scored during that four-run inning.

San Diego erupted for 10 runs in the eighth, capitalizing on three Pacific errors and 14 walks. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Sim]] drew a bases-loaded walk in the rally, while [[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] earned the win with a scoreless inning of relief.

Pacific erased an early two-run deficit and beat San Diego 5–2 at Fowler Park behind a complete-game victory from Grant Stevens. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] and [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] supplied the Toreros’ two runs, with DeCriscio’s solo homer in the third briefly giving San Diego a 2–0 lead.

The Tigers tied it in the fourth, then took command in the sixth when Tony Otis tripled home two runs and later scored on Jack Metcho’s sacrifice fly. [[cb-pacific-chase-graves|Chase Graves]] added a hit, was hit by a pitch and stole a base as Pacific’s offense turned its five runs into the decisive margin.

Stevens closed the door by allowing eight hits and two runs over nine innings, striking out five. [[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] and [[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Austin Smith]] combined for three scoreless relief innings for San Diego, but Pacific’s sixth-inning push stood up.

player_of_game.name: Grant Stevens
player_of_game.line: W, CG — 9.0 IP, 8 H, 2 R, 3 BB, 5 K

paragraphs: Cal State Northridge held off San Diego 12–10 at Matador Field, surviving a late Torero rally after building an 11–4 lead through five innings. [[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Austin Smith]] went 2-for-3 with a home run, five RBIs, a walk, a hit by pitch and a stolen base in the loss.

San Diego struck first on Smith’s two-run single and added two more in the third, but CSUN answered with three runs in the second before taking control with four in the fourth. [[cb-cal-state-northridge-graysen-tarlow|Graysen Tarlow]] delivered a two-run double, and [[cb-cal-state-northridge-kevin-fitzer|Kevin Fitzer]] followed with a two-run homer in that inning.

The Toreros scored twice in each of the final three innings, capped by Smith’s two-run homer in the ninth, but could not get closer. [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] went 3-for-4 with a double and a walk, while Ryan Wentz earned the win for CSUN.

Pepperdine pulled away for an 8–3 win over San Diego at Fowler Park after the teams traded early swings. [[cb-pepperdine-ryan-johnson|Ryan Johnson]] put the Waves ahead with a two-run first-inning homer, went 1-for-3 with three runs and two walks, and later scored the game’s final run.

San Diego answered with three in the second as [[cb-san-diego-jack-gurevitch|Jack Gurevitch]] tripled home two and [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] brought him home on a sacrifice fly. Pepperdine reclaimed the lead in the sixth on RBI singles by Jack Basseer and Greg Mehlhaff, then added one in the seventh and two in the ninth.

Shane Telfer earned the win by limiting the Toreros to three runs over six innings, and Jack Baird finished with three scoreless innings for the save. [[cb-san-diego-james-sashin|James Sashin]] struck out five across 5.2 innings for San Diego, but Pepperdine’s bullpen protected the lead.

San Diego erased a four-run first-inning deficit and beat Pepperdine 8–4 at Fowler Park. [[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Austin Smith]] delivered the turning point with a seventh-inning grand slam, then finished the game on the mound for the win.

The Toreros chipped away with James Arakawa’s first-inning homer, an Ariel Armas RBI groundout in the second, and two fourth-inning runs to tie it. [[cb-san-diego-jack-gurevitch|Jack Gurevitch]] went 2-for-3 with a walk and scored twice, while Armas finished 2-for-3 with two RBIs.

Smith entered in the sixth and retired the Waves over 3.2 scoreless innings, striking out six while allowing no hits. [[cb-san-diego-garrett-rennie|Garrett Rennie]] kept the deficit manageable through 5.1 innings, setting the stage for San Diego’s four-run seventh.

player_of_game.name: Austin Smith
player_of_game.line: 1-for-4, HR, 4 RBI; W, 3.2 IP, 0 H, 0 R, 6 K

paragraphs: San Diego held off Pepperdine 7–6 to take the series at Fowler Park, surviving a three-run ninth-inning rally. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] gave the Toreros an early cushion with a two-run first-inning homer, and [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] drove in another run in the third.

Pepperdine cut the margin to 5–3, but [[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Austin Smith]] delivered a two-run double in the eighth after reaching base five times. [[cb-pepperdine-john-peck|John Peck]] doubled home a run in the seventh and was part of the Waves’ final-inning pressure, but San Diego stayed in front.

[[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] earned the win with 2.2 hitless, scoreless innings and five strikeouts, a key bridge for the Toreros after the early starter. Nick Suspenzi got the final two outs for his first save after Pepperdine brought the tying run to third.

player_of_game.name: Ivran Romero
player_of_game.line: W, 2.2 IP, 0 H, 0 R, 1 BB, 5 K

paragraphs: San Diego broke a 2–2 tie with three runs in the ninth and beat UC San Diego 5–2 at Triton Ballpark. [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] homered in the second, then added a sacrifice fly in the decisive ninth to finish 2-for-4 with two RBIs.

The Toreros carried a 2–0 lead before UC San Diego tied it on a third-inning fielder’s-choice RBI and a run home on a wild pitch in the fourth. [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] opened the ninth-inning scoring with an RBI double, and [[cb-san-diego-jack-gurevitch|Jack Gurevitch]] followed with an RBI single.

San Diego used nine pitchers and limited the Tritons to three hits. [[cb-san-diego-mikiah-negrete|Mikiah Negrete]] earned the win with 1.1 innings of scoreless relief and two strikeouts, while [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] reached three times, scored once and drove in an early run.

San Diego opened its Spokane series with an 8–1 win over Gonzaga, scoring four times in the first inning and never trailing. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] drove in a run during the opening rally, then added a solo homer in the third as the Toreros built a 5–0 lead.

[[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Austin Smith]] was dominant on the mound, allowing two hits over five scoreless innings with nine strikeouts to earn the win; he also singled home two runs in the first. [[cb-san-diego-ryan-kysar|Ryan Kysar]] followed with two scoreless innings, keeping Gonzaga hitless through seven.

San Diego added solo homers from [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] and [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]], while Angelo Peraza had two hits and an RBI. Gonzaga’s only run came on Enzo Apodaca’s eighth-inning homer before [[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] closed the victory with 1.1 scoreless innings.

player_of_game.name: Austin Smith
player_of_game.line: W, 5.0 IP, 2 H, 0 R, 4 BB, 9 K; 1-for-4, RBI

paragraphs: Gonzaga edged San Diego 3–2 in Spokane, turning a low-scoring series game on two third-inning runs and an unearned eighth-inning insurance run. [[cb-san-diego-jack-costello|Jack Costello]] accounted for San Diego’s first run with a sixth-inning RBI triple and finished 2-for-4 with a double and triple.

The Toreros had 10 hits but left 10 runners on base against starter Matthew Mueller and closer Ty Buckner. James Arakawa went 4-for-4, while [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] walked twice before scoring on a ninth-inning wild pitch that brought San Diego within one.

[[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] kept the game within reach with 3.1 innings of one-run relief, striking out five without a walk. [[cb-san-diego-james-sashin|James Sashin]] took the loss after allowing two runs over 4.2 innings as Gonzaga held on for the series-evening win.

San Diego took the Gonzaga series with a 9–3 win in Spokane, opening with three first-inning runs and never surrendering the lead. San Diego received solo homers from [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] in the second and [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] in the sixth, but managed only four hits overall. Portland outlasted San Diego 8–7 at Fowler Park after a wild first inning and a late bullpen lock-down. [[cb-portland-jake-holcroft|Jake Holcroft]] went 3-for-5 with a home run and three RBIs, including a two-run homer in the second that put the Pilots back in front for good.

San Diego answered Portland’s four-run first with five runs of its own, highlighted by [[cb-san-diego-jack-gurevitch|Jack Gurevitch]]’s two-run single and [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]]’s two-run homer. The Toreros pulled within one on [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]]’s sacrifice fly in the sixth, but Jacob Dobmeier held San Diego to one hit over the final four innings for the save. Portland clinched the series with a 9–5 win over San Diego, launching four home runs and building an 8–1 lead through five innings. [[cb-san-diego-ariel-armas|Ariel Armas]] paced the Toreros’ late response, going 2-for-4 with a solo homer in the eighth.

San Diego erased a four-run deficit and walked off Portland 7–6 at Fowler Park. [[cb-san-diego-jack-gurevitch|Jack Gurevitch]] went 2-for-3 with two RBIs and two walks, then singled home Kevin Sim in the ninth to finish the comeback.

Portland seized a 3–0 first-inning lead on Zach Toglia’s three-run homer and extended it to 6–2 by the seventh. The Aztecs’ pitching staff limited San Diego to two hits and struck out nine. [[cb-san-diego-kevin-sim|Kevin Sim]] and [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] recorded the Toreros’ only hits, but neither side produced another extra-base hit or a run after the opening frame.

San Diego scored nine runs in the first inning and rolled past San Francisco 17–3 at Fowler Park. [[cb-san-diego-jack-gurevitch|Jack Gurevitch]] went 2-for-6 with two home runs and five RBIs, capping the opening outburst with a three-run shot before adding another two-run homer in the seventh.

San Diego rallied with three late runs to edge San Francisco 6–5 at Fowler Park. [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] went 3-for-5 with two RBIs, delivering the walk-off RBI single in the ninth after Dustin Allen’s fielder’s-choice grounder tied the game.

The Toreros jumped ahead on first-inning home runs from [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] and [[cb-san-diego-jack-gurevitch|Jack Gurevitch]], but San Francisco answered with four runs in the third and a Mattie Thomas homer in the sixth. San Diego completed the sweep of San Francisco with a 9–7 win at Fowler Park. [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] went 3-for-4 with an RBI and a walk, setting the table throughout a 10-hit Toreros offense.

The teams traded two-run frames early before San Diego broke the 4–4 tie in the fifth. San Francisco closed to within two on Will Asby’s second home run of the game, but Aídan Gonzalez retired the side in order in the ninth for his first save. [[cb-san-diego-ariel-armas|Ariel Armas]]’s two-run homer in the second, [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]]’s RBI single, and a win from Ryan Kysar helped San Diego finish the series sweep.

Cal State Northridge broke a 2–2 tie with four runs in the eighth and beat San Diego 7–4 at Fowler Park. [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] led the Toreros at the plate, going 3-for-5 with a triple and an RBI.

CSUN used two hit-by-pitches and Kevin Fitzer’s two-run hit to take control in the eighth, then added a run in the ninth. [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] doubled home a run in San Diego’s eighth-inning response, but Joshua Romero struck out three over 1.1 scoreless innings to close it.

San Diego opened its series at Loyola Marymount with an 11–1 victory behind [[cb-san-diego-ariel-armas|Ariel Armas]]’s five RBIs. Armas went 2-for-4 with two doubles, driving in three during a fifth-inning surge and two more in the seventh.

[[cb-san-diego-jack-gurevitch|Jack Gurevitch]] set the tone with a two-run first-inning homer, while [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] went 3-for-5 with a double and an RBI. [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] added three hits as the Toreros turned 12 hits into 11 runs.

San Diego’s pitching staff navigated 11 LMU hits while allowing only one run. [[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] earned the win with two scoreless innings and five strikeouts, while [[cb-san-diego-ryan-kysar|Ryan Kysar]] gave the Toreros three scoreless innings to start the game.

San Diego beat Loyola Marymount 6–3 as [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] provided the decisive swing. Worthington went 1-for-3 with a two-run homer in the eighth, putting the Toreros back in front after LMU had erased a three-run deficit.

San Diego scored twice in the fourth and added a run in the fifth before LMU tied it in the seventh. [[cb-san-diego-james-arakawa|James Arakawa]] went 2-for-4 with a double and two runs, and [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] drove in the fifth-inning run.

[[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] earned the win after allowing two runs, one earned, over two innings. [[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] closed with a perfect ninth and two strikeouts for his first save.

Loyola Marymount rallied past San Diego 10–9 in a back-and-forth series finale. [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] went 4-for-4 with a double, a homer, two RBIs and a walk, fueling the Toreros’ offense from the bottom half of the order.

San Diego fought back from an early three-run deficit with four runs in the fourth, then regained the lead in the sixth on Worthington’s homer and [[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Austin Smith]]’s two-run single. Smith finished 3-for-5 with four RBIs, while [[cb-san-diego-james-arakawa|James Arakawa]] scored three runs.

The Toreros took a 9–8 lead into the bottom of the eighth, but LMU tied it on Grant Weiss’ RBI single and won on Sam Biller’s bases-loaded walk. [[cb-san-diego-ariel-armas|Ariel Armas]] added two hits and an RBI in San Diego’s 15-hit effort.

BYU used a four-run first and six-run third to beat San Diego 10–6 at Fowler Park. [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]] drove in half of the Toreros’ runs, going 2-for-5 with a double and three RBIs.

Ozzie Pratt homered in the first and added an RBI single in BYU’s third-inning outburst, while Austin Deming’s three-run homer made it 10–1. San Diego kept battling: Gabe D'Arcy went 2-for-5 with a double and two RBIs, and [[cb-san-diego-james-arakawa|James Arakawa]] had two hits, two runs and an RBI.

San Diego’s bullpen held BYU scoreless over the final six innings, including two scoreless frames from James Sashin and a clean inning apiece from Aídan Gonzalez, Mikiah Negrete, Nick Suspenzi and Drake Frize. [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] reached twice and scored two runs in the loss.

San Diego answered BYU’s opening-game win with an 8–4 victory at Fowler Park. [[cb-san-diego-jack-gurevitch|Jack Gurevitch]] broke the game open with a three-run homer in the third, finishing 1-for-3 with three RBIs and a walk.

[[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] went 2-for-4 with two runs and an RBI, while Austin Smith reached three times and drove in two.

[[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] earned the win by holding BYU to three runs over five innings with four strikeouts after Ryan Robinson’s four-inning start. The Toreros’ six-run cushion proved enough despite BYU’s late scoring.

[[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Austin Smith]] struck out 11 over 6.2 innings as San Diego beat BYU 5–1. Smith allowed four hits and one run without a walk, then added a hit and a walk as the Toreros completed the series win.

San Diego broke through with a fourth-inning sacrifice fly, then took control when [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] tripled home two runs in the sixth. Peraza finished 1-for-2 with three RBIs, a walk and a run scored.

The Matadors scored in each of the first two innings, then used Ali Camarillo’s homer in the fourth to extend the lead. CSUN’s seven-run seventh featured Mason Le’s two-run homer and Kevin Fitzer’s three-run homer before Jakob Simons added a solo shot in the eighth.

UC San Diego managed only three hits and did not produce an extra-base hit. [[cb-uc-san-diego-jalen-smith|Jalen Smith]] went 1-for-2 with a walk, while Michael Mitchell absorbed the loss after allowing two runs, one earned, in two innings.

UC Irvine rallied from an early two-run deficit and beat San Diego 10–2 at Fowler Park. [[cb-uc-irvine-anthony-martinez|Anthony Martinez]] went 4-for-6 with a three-run homer in a six-run eighth inning that put the game away.

San Diego scored unearned runs in the first and second, but UC Irvine tied it in the fifth and moved in front in the sixth. [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] went 2-for-4 with a run scored, while [[cb-san-diego-james-arakawa|James Arakawa]] added a hit for the Toreros.

The Anteaters piled up 16 hits, with Chase Call recording three and Anthony Martinez, Dub Gleed, Luke Spillane and Auggie Gutierrez each producing multiple hits. San Diego reliever Tristan LaMaison took the loss after the fifth-inning rally.

San Diego held off Saint Mary’s 4–3 in Moraga behind [[cb-san-diego-james-arakawa|James Arakawa]]’s three-hit game. Arakawa went 3-for-5 with two runs, a double and a stolen base as the Toreros claimed the series opener.

[[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] went 3-for-5 with a double, triple, RBI and run scored, while [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] added two hits, an RBI and a stolen base. Austin Smith’s seventh-inning RBI single gave San Diego the eventual winning margin.

[[cb-san-diego-ryan-robinson|Ryan Robinson]] earned the win with 5.2 innings of one-run ball, and [[cb-san-diego-ivran-romero|Ivran Romero]] stranded the tying threat before finishing two scoreless innings for his first save. Saint Mary’s rallied on home runs from Gavin Napier and Coleman Schmidt, but could not draw even.

Saint Mary’s blanked San Diego 6–0 as [[cb-saint-mary-s-gavin-napier|Gavin Napier]] started the scoring with a first-inning solo homer. Napier went 2-for-4 with an RBI and a walk in the Gaels’ wire-to-wire victory.

Saint Mary’s scored three times in the first and never trailed, receiving two RBIs from Blake McDonald and three runs scored from Christian Almanza. Gabe D'Arcy and [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] accounted for two of San Diego’s four hits.

Ryan Wiltse earned the win with five scoreless innings, while the Saint Mary’s bullpen completed the four-hit shutout. [[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Austin Smith]] took the loss after allowing five runs, four earned, over 3.1 innings.

San Diego held off Saint Mary’s 10–8 in Moraga behind a huge afternoon from [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]], who went 2-for-3 with two home runs, two runs scored and three RBIs. Allen’s fourth-inning solo shot and sixth-inning inside-the-park two-run homer pushed the Toreros ahead for good.

[[cb-san-diego-jack-gurevitch|Jack Gurevitch]] went 3-for-5 with a double, triple and two RBIs, while [[cb-san-diego-austin-smith|Austin Smith]] delivered a two-run single in the first. [[cb-san-diego-justin-decriscio|Justin DeCriscio]] scored twice and stole home in San Diego’s four-run sixth.

Saint Mary’s cut the deficit to two on a three-run homer by Dalton Mashore in the sixth and a Nate Chong homer in the seventh, but could get no closer. [[cb-san-diego-ryan-kysar|Ryan Kysar]] earned the win with four scoreless innings, and [[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] worked a scoreless ninth for the save.

Santa Clara beat Gonzaga 4–2 at Las Vegas Ballpark in the WCC Tournament, with [[cb-santa-clara-coleman-brigman|Coleman Brigman]] supplying the decisive offense. Brigman’s two-run homer in the fourth put the Broncos ahead, and his RBI single in the eighth restored their two-run cushion after Gonzaga rallied.

Cade Pilchard held Gonzaga scoreless through five innings, allowing four hits with two strikeouts, before Skylar Hales finished the final four innings for the save. Efrain Manzo went 3-for-4 with two runs scored, while Ben Steck added a solo homer in the seventh.

Gonzaga collected 10 hits but did its scoring in the eighth, when Sam Stem singled home [[cb-gonzaga-brian-kalmer|Brian Kalmer]] and Tommy Eisenstat added an RBI fielder’s choice. [[cb-gonzaga-owen-wild|Owen Wild]] struck out seven over 7.1 innings in the loss.

Saint Mary’s erupted for eight ninth-inning runs and routed San Diego 17–8 at Las Vegas Ballpark in the WCC Tournament. [[cb-saint-mary-s-coleman-schmidt|Coleman Schmidt]] powered the Gaels by going 3-for-6 with two home runs, two runs and five RBIs, including a three-run shot in the first and a two-run blast in the third.

Christian Almanza went 3-for-3 with a homer, four runs and three RBIs, while Bill Ralston finished 4-for-6 with three runs and two RBIs. Eddie Madrigal homered and drove in three, then added a two-run single in the ninth as Saint Mary’s turned a four-run lead into a rout.

San Diego answered with 13 hits, including two hits apiece from [[cb-san-diego-angelo-peraza|Angelo Peraza]] and [[cb-san-diego-ariel-armas|Ariel Armas]], but never got closer than four after the fourth. Connor Linchey earned the win with six innings, and the Gaels’ offense finished with 17 hits.

No. 12 Duke opened its 2024 season with a 6–3 victory over Indiana at Springs Brooks Stadium behind [[cb-duke-jonathan-santucci|Jonathan Santucci]]. The left-hander worked five scoreless innings, allowed four hits, walked two and struck out seven to earn the win.

Duke’s offense broke through in the fifth on Wallace Clark’s RBI double, then Alex Stone and Logan Bravo hit back-to-back solo home runs in the sixth. Bravo went 3-for-5 with a homer and two RBIs, while Stone drove in two with his homer and seventh-inning sacrifice fly.

Indiana answered with home runs from [[cb-indiana-tyler-cerny|Tyler Cerny]] and [[cb-indiana-carter-mathison|Carter Mathison]], but [[cb-duke-charlie-beilenson|Charlie Beilenson]] shut the door. Beilenson allowed one hit over 2.2 scoreless innings, struck out five and recorded his first save of the season.

Coastal Carolina opened its season with a 26–0 rout of George Mason at Springs Brooks Stadium, with [[cb-coastal-carolina-derek-bender|Derek Bender]] leading a 15-hit attack. Bender went 2-for-6 with a home run, three runs and six RBIs, including a grand slam in the third that put the Chanticleers ahead 12–0.

Coastal scored six times in the first and seven more in the third, then added six in the fourth. Caden Bodine went 3-for-4 with three runs and three RBIs, Sam Antonacci scored three times and drove in three, while Jake Books, Zack Beach and Bender each homered.

[[cb-coastal-carolina-riley-eikhoff|Riley Eikhoff]] carried a no-hitter through six innings, allowing no runs or walks and striking out three. Hayden Johnson completed the one-hitter, with George Mason’s Derek Wood accounting for the Patriots’ only hit.

No. 12 Duke overwhelmed George Mason 23–5 at Springs Brooks Stadium, highlighted by a historic power display from [[cb-duke-aj-gracia|AJ Gracia]]. Gracia went 4-for-5 with three home runs, three runs and nine RBIs, blasting three-run homers in the first, second and seventh innings.

Duke hit nine home runs in all and scored eight times in the first. Devin Obee homered twice, Zac Morris hit two home runs and drove in four, while Ben Miller, Alex Stone, Wallace Clark and Chase Krewson also went deep in the 23-hit attack.

[[cb-duke-kyle-johnson|Kyle Johnson]] earned the win with three scoreless innings of relief, allowing one hit. George Mason received a leadoff homer and two RBIs from South Trimble, plus a two-run double from Jordan Smith, but could not recover from Duke’s opening-inning avalanche.

Indiana beat Coastal Carolina 7–2 at Springs Brooks Stadium, taking control with two runs in the fifth and breaking it open with four in the ninth. [[cb-indiana-aj-shepard|AJ Shepard]] supplied the biggest late hit, a two-run homer in the ninth, while [[cb-indiana-brandon-burckel|Brandon Burckel]] hit a solo homer in the eighth.

[[cb-indiana-ty-bothwell|Ty Bothwell]] earned the win with five innings of two-run ball; both Coastal Carolina runs were unearned. Connor Foley set the tone with four scoreless innings and seven strikeouts, and Indiana’s staff combined for 10 strikeouts.

Coastal Carolina tied the game in the sixth on RBI hits by Graham Brown and Dean Mihos, but Indiana answered immediately. [[cb-indiana-tyler-cerny|Tyler Cerny]] went 2-for-4 with two RBIs, while Devin Taylor, Brock Tibbitts and Burckel each drove in runs.

Indiana finished the Conway weekend with a 9–3 win over George Mason, getting three early runs from home runs by [[cb-indiana-aj-shepard|AJ Shepard]] and Morgan Colopy. [[cb-indiana-carter-mathison|Carter Mathison]] then delivered the decisive blow in the eighth, a three-run homer that stretched the lead from two to five.

Mathison finished with two runs and three RBIs, while Josh Pyne went 3-for-6 and [[cb-indiana-devin-taylor|Devin Taylor]] added two hits and an RBI. Indiana totaled 12 hits and took advantage of two Mason errors in the opening inning.

Seti Manase earned the win with 2.1 innings of relief, allowing one unearned run, and Julian Tonghini closed with three scoreless innings for the save. George Mason’s James Quinn-Irons went 2-for-4 with an RBI, but Indiana’s bullpen limited the Patriots to four hits.

No. 12 Duke completed a 4–0 opening weekend with a 5–3 win over Coastal Carolina at Springs Brooks Stadium. [[cb-duke-aidan-weaver|Aidan Weaver]] earned the win in his Duke debut, allowing one unearned run over 2.1 innings while striking out four.

Zac Morris opened the scoring with a first-inning homer, and Ben Miller went 3-for-5 with a two-run homer in the third. Logan Bravo added an RBI single that inning, then Wallace Clark’s sixth-inning RBI double supplied Duke’s final run.

Coastal Carolina managed only four hits, with Caden Bodine going 2-for-3 with an RBI. [[cb-duke-charlie-beilenson|Charlie Beilenson]] retired all seven batters he faced over 2.1 scoreless innings, striking out two for the save.

College of Charleston held off Marshall 8–5 at Patriots Point, answering the Thundering Herd’s three-run sixth with runs in each of the final three innings. [[cb-college-of-charleston-emmett-bice|Emmett Bice]] was pivotal in relief, working 2.2 scoreless innings with four strikeouts after Marshall had tied the game.

Luke Wood went 2-for-4 with two runs and an RBI, scoring in Charleston’s four-run fourth and again on Dylan Johnson’s seventh-inning RBI double. Kevin Madden reached three times with three hits and two runs, while Cole Mathis broke the sixth-inning tie with an RBI double.

Marshall received three hits and two RBIs from Chase Kaiser and two RBIs from Giovanni Ferraro, who helped erase a 5–2 deficit in the sixth. [[cb-college-of-charleston-davis-aiken|Davis Aiken]] then pitched a perfect ninth for his second save.

No. 8 Clemson pulled away from Presbyterian for an 8–2 win at Doug Kingsmore Stadium, breaking a 3–2 game open with five runs in the seventh. [[cb-clemson-jarren-purify|Jarren Purify]] delivered the decisive swing, a grand slam that capped the inning.

[[cb-clemson-cam-cannarella|Cam Cannarella]] went 3-for-5 with a first-inning home run and an RBI, while Jimmy Obertop finished 3-for-5 with a homer, double and two RBIs. Clemson had 10 hits and drew seven walks in the victory.

Presbyterian led 2–1 after the third before Obertop’s solo homer tied it and his RBI single in the fourth gave Clemson the lead. Joe Allen earned the win with four innings of two-run ball, while Clemson’s final two relievers combined for three scoreless innings.

No. 21 South Carolina beat Queens 13–3 at Founders Park, scoring four runs in the first and five in the fourth. [[cb-south-carolina-cole-messina|Cole Messina]] opened the scoring with a three-run homer and finished with three RBIs, while Ethan Petry added a homer, two hits and three runs.

Ryan Bakes went 3-for-4 with a double and three RBIs, and Will Tippett reached base five times with three walks, two RBIs and a hit by pitch. South Carolina drew 15 walks and capitalized on five Queens errors.

[[cb-south-carolina-matthew-becker|Matthew Becker]] earned the win, striking out five over two scoreless innings. Queens got solo home runs from JJ Sousa, Tyler Cotto and Connor Manco, but the Gamecocks’ staff struck out 17.

[[cb-wichita-state-derek-williams|Derek Williams]] gave Wichita State a 4–3 lead in the 10th with a solo homer, but [[cb-virginia-henry-ford|Henry Ford]] answered in the bottom half with a two-run walk-off double that scored [[cb-virginia-anthony-stephan|Anthony Stephan]] and [[cb-virginia-bobby-whalen|Bobby Whalen]] for Virginia’s 5–4 win.

The Shockers had built a 3–1 edge on [[cb-wichita-state-darnell-parker|Darnell Parker Jr.]]’s solo homer and [[cb-wichita-state-ryan-callahan|Ryan Callahan]]’s RBI single in the fifth. [[cb-virginia-bobby-whalen|Whalen]] tied it with an RBI single in the sixth, and Virginia drew even again on an eighth-inning error before Ford’s deciding swing.

[[cb-virginia-aidan-teel|Aidan Teel]] earned the win with two innings of one-run relief and five strikeouts. Wichita State starter [[cb-wichita-state-caden-favors|Caden Favors]] limited Virginia to one earned run across 6.2 innings while striking out seven, but the Cavaliers completed the 10-inning comeback.

Auburn erased a 3–2 deficit with three runs in the seventh, starting with [[cb-auburn-mason-maners|Mason Maners]]’ tying solo homer before [[cb-auburn-bobby-peirce|Bobby Peirce]] launched the go-ahead two-run shot in a 7–5 win over Iowa.

[[cb-auburn-christian-hall|Christian Hall]] supplied a two-out RBI single in the sixth, then added a solo homer in the eighth as Auburn built its four-run cushion. Iowa had taken its early lead on [[cb-iowa-blake-guerin|Blake Guerin]]’s RBI walk, [[cb-iowa-kyle-huckstorf|Kyle Huckstorf]]’s RBI single and [[cb-iowa-michael-seegers|Michael Seegers]]’ sacrifice bunt.

[[cb-auburn-cam-tilly|Cam Tilly]] worked two scoreless innings with three strikeouts for his first collegiate win after [[cb-auburn-john-armstrong|John Armstrong]] delivered 2.2 scoreless relief innings. [[cb-iowa-brody-brecht|Brody Brecht]] struck out 11 across six innings for Iowa, which got within 7–5 on [[cb-iowa-sam-petersen|Sam Petersen]]’s two-run ninth-inning homer.

[[cb-auburn-cooper-mcmurray|Cooper McMurray]] blasted a first-inning grand slam and finished with two hits and six RBI as Auburn rolled to a 19–8 seven-inning victory over Wichita State. [[cb-auburn-bobby-peirce|Bobby Peirce]] added a two-run homer in the second and went 2-for-4 with three RBI.

Auburn scored at least four runs in four of its first six turns, piling up 19 on 10 hits while drawing 16 walks. [[cb-auburn-ike-irish|Ike Irish]] scored four times, while [[cb-auburn-deric-fabian|Deric Fabian]] cleared the bases with a three-run double in the sixth to complete the Tigers’ scoring.

Wichita State answered the early 7–0 deficit with [[cb-wichita-state-dayvin-johnson|Dayvin Johnson]]’s three-run homer, and [[cb-wichita-state-derek-williams|Derek Williams]] drove in another during the five-run fifth. [[cb-auburn-joseph-gonzalez|Joseph Gonzalez]] earned the win with four innings, and Auburn’s early surge made the late Shocker runs immaterial.

[[cb-virginia-casey-saucke|Casey Saucke]] went 3-for-6 with a homer and four RBI, helping Virginia erase a six-run first-inning deficit for a 12–9 comeback over Iowa. His seventh-inning homer tied the game, and his two-out single later in the inning gave the Cavaliers their first lead.

Iowa opened with six runs, but Virginia answered with a five-run fourth capped by [[cb-virginia-ethan-anderson|Ethan Anderson]]’s two-run homer. After Iowa tied it at 9–9 in the eighth, [[cb-virginia-anthony-stephan|Anthony Stephan]] drew a bases-loaded walk in the ninth before [[cb-virginia-henry-ford|Henry Ford]] drove in two more with a single.

[[cb-virginia-jay-woolfolk|Jay Woolfolk]] delivered 4.1 scoreless relief innings with five strikeouts after the difficult first, then [[cb-virginia-blake-barker|Blake Barker]] worked around a ninth-inning walk for his first save. [[cb-virginia-henry-godbout|Henry Godbout]] added four hits as Virginia completed its second straight comeback win.

Wichita State erased a 5–0 deficit with a dozen runs over the final four innings, beating Iowa 12–6 behind three-run homers from [[cb-wichita-state-josh-livingston|Josh Livingston]], [[cb-wichita-state-seth-stroh|Seth Stroh]] and [[cb-wichita-state-jordan-rogers|Jordan Rogers]].

[[cb-wichita-state-derek-williams|Derek Williams]] went 3-for-4 with two runs and sparked the sixth-inning comeback with a leadoff double. In the seventh, his ground-rule double set up the tie before [[cb-wichita-state-jaden-gustafson|Jaden Gustafson]] singled him home and Stroh’s three-run shot turned a 5–5 game into an 8–5 Shocker lead.

Stroh then preserved the lead with an inning-ending outfield assist at the plate, cutting down Iowa’s [[cb-iowa-kyle-huckstorf|Kyle Huckstorf]]. [[cb-wichita-state-ryan-geraghty|Ryan Geraghty]] recorded the final out of the sixth for his first collegiate win, while [[cb-wichita-state-brady-hamilton|Brady Hamilton]] fired 2.2 scoreless innings with three strikeouts for his first save.

[[cb-virginia-kevin-jaxel|Kevin Jaxel]] earned the win with 2.2 innings of one-run relief as Virginia completed the Jax College Classic sweep with a 6–4 win over Auburn. [[cb-virginia-aidan-teel|Aidan Teel]] followed with a scoreless ninth for his third save.

Virginia scored in four of its final five turns after Auburn briefly led 2–1. [[cb-virginia-luke-hanson|Luke Hanson]]’s sixth-inning RBI double put the Cavaliers ahead for good, and [[cb-virginia-casey-saucke|Casey Saucke]] doubled home [[cb-virginia-ethan-anderson|Ethan Anderson]] in the seventh to make it 4–2.

After Auburn pulled within one, [[cb-virginia-bobby-whalen|Bobby Whalen]] opened the eighth with a ground-rule double for the fifth run, and [[cb-virginia-anthony-stephan|Anthony Stephan]] added a two-out RBI single. [[cb-virginia-griff-o-ferrall|Griff O’Ferrall]], Stephan and [[cb-virginia-harrison-didawick|Harrison Didawick]] all finished with two hits.

[[cb-north-carolina-jason-decaro|Jason DeCaro]] carried a no-hit bid into the sixth and earned his first collegiate win as North Carolina handled VCU 8–2. The freshman retired the first 14 Rams, then finished six innings with three strikeouts, three hits and one run allowed.

North Carolina seized control with four first-inning runs, punctuated by [[cb-north-carolina-anthony-donofrio|Anthony Donofrio]]’s bases-loaded double. [[cb-north-carolina-luke-stevenson|Luke Stevenson]] went 3-for-3 with a triple and RBI, while [[cb-north-carolina-casey-cook|Casey Cook]] and [[cb-north-carolina-alex-madera|Alex Madera]] each added two hits.

The Tar Heels built the margin to 8–0 on Cook’s RBI triple and [[cb-north-carolina-alberto-osuna|Alberto Osuna]]’s RBI single. [[cb-vcu-aden-hill|Aden Hill]] and [[cb-vcu-chris-mchugh|Chris McHugh]] drove in the Rams’ late runs, but North Carolina’s bullpen completed the win with three scoreless innings.

[[cb-nc-state-drew-lanphere|Drew Lanphere]] went 3-for-5 with two homers, four RBI and three runs as NC State routed Queens 17–2. His first career homer came in the fourth, and he added another two-run shot during the Wolfpack’s six-run fifth.

Queens scored first, but NC State immediately batted around for eight runs in the bottom of the first. [[cb-nc-state-alec-makarewicz|Alec Makarewicz]]’s two-run double put the Wolfpack ahead for good, while [[cb-nc-state-luke-nixon|Luke Nixon]] and [[cb-nc-state-josh-hogue|Josh Hogue]] added two-run singles.

Makarewicz finished 3-for-4 with a homer and four RBI, and [[cb-nc-state-cooper-consiglio|Cooper Consiglio]] won his first NC State start with four innings of two-run ball and three strikeouts. The bullpen blanked Queens over the final five innings.

[[cb-southeastern-louisiana-brennan-stuprich|Brennan Stuprich]] worked seven scoreless innings, allowing three hits and one walk while striking out five, as Southeastern Louisiana opened the Keith LeClair Classic with a 5–1 win over Cal State Fullerton.

[[cb-southeastern-louisiana-justin-williams|Justin Williams]] homered in the second, then [[cb-southeastern-louisiana-shea-thomas|Shea Thomas]] broke the game open in the fifth with a two-run homer and added an RBI double in the seventh. Thomas finished 3-for-3 with three RBI, while Williams went 3-for-3 with a homer, double and two RBI.

Cal State Fullerton had runners in scoring position in each of the first two innings, but Stuprich escaped both threats. [[cb-cal-state-fullerton-moises-guzman|Moises Guzman]] finally put the Titans on the board with an eighth-inning solo homer, but [[cb-southeastern-louisiana-jackson-rodriguez|Jackson Rodriguez]] closed the final two innings.

[[cb-east-carolina-trey-yesavage|Trey Yesavage]] delivered a career-best eight scoreless innings, allowing two hits and striking out 11 as East Carolina beat Purdue 7–1 in the Keith LeClair Classic opener.

The Pirates struck first in the third when [[cb-east-carolina-ryley-johnson|Ryley Johnson]] singled home a run before [[cb-east-carolina-carter-cunningham|Carter Cunningham]] drilled a two-run homer. [[cb-east-carolina-dixon-williams|Dixon Williams]] added a solo homer in the fourth as ECU built a 4–0 lead.

ECU added three eighth-inning runs on Cunningham’s sacrifice fly, [[cb-east-carolina-jacob-starling|Jacob Starling]]’s RBI single and Williams’ RBI groundout. Purdue’s [[cb-purdue-logan-sutter|Logan Sutter]] broke up the shutout with a ninth-inning homer, but [[cb-east-carolina-jackson-dilorenzo|Jackson DiLorenzo]] finished the win.

[[cb-unc-asheville-justin-needles|Justin Needles]] settled UNC Asheville after Siena took a 6–5 lead in the fifth, allowing one run over five innings while striking out five to earn the win in an 11–6 comeback.

[[cb-siena-kobe-stenson|Kobe Stenson]]’s three-run homer highlighted Siena’s four-run fourth, and [[cb-siena-louis-percival|Louis Percival]] drove in the go-ahead run in the fifth. Asheville answered immediately when [[cb-unc-asheville-ben-hemphill|Ben Hemphill]] ripped a two-run double, putting the Bulldogs back in front for good.

UNC Asheville kept adding on: [[cb-unc-asheville-michael-groves|Michael Groves]] doubled home a sixth-inning run, then [[cb-unc-asheville-corbin-lanowitz|Corbin Lanowitz]] and [[cb-unc-asheville-ty-kaufman|Ty Kaufman]] combined for three seventh-inning RBI. Kaufman finished 3-for-4 with three RBI, while [[cb-unc-asheville-cameron-johnson|Cameron Johnson]] scored three runs.

[[cb-florida-state-jamie-arnold|Jamie Arnold]] gave Florida State six scoreless innings, allowing seven hits without a walk and striking out seven as the Seminoles beat Michigan State 11–2 at Fluor Field.

Florida State built its lead with two runs in the second and a third-inning [[cb-florida-state-daniel-cantu|Daniel Cantu]] RBI single. [[cb-florida-state-cam-smith|Cam Smith]] then circled the bases for an inside-the-park, two-run homer in the sixth, and [[cb-florida-state-jaime-ferrer|Jaime Ferrer]] added a solo shot in the eighth.

The Seminoles turned Michigan State’s five errors into extra separation late. [[cb-florida-state-mcgwire-holbrook|McGwire Holbrook]] went 3-for-5 with two RBI, while [[cb-florida-state-marco-dinges|Marco Dinges]] scored three times. Michigan State finally broke through for two eighth-inning runs on RBI doubles by [[cb-michigan-state-ryan-mckay|Ryan McKay]] and [[cb-michigan-state-dillon-kark|Dillon Kark]].

[[cb-illinois-vytas-valincius|Vytas Valincius]] powered Illinois’ four-run first with a two-run double, then added an RBI single in the seventh as the Illini held an early 6–2 advantage over Western Michigan.

Western Michigan rallied to tie it in the eighth. [[cb-western-michigan-dylan-nevar|Dylan Nevar]] hit a two-run homer in the fourth, [[cb-western-michigan-josh-swinehart|Josh Swinehart]] added a solo shot in the seventh, and [[cb-western-michigan-cj-richmond|CJ Richmond]] blasted a three-run homer to make it 6–6.

Illinois reclaimed the lead in the 10th when [[cb-illinois-coltin-quagliano|Coltin Quagliano]] tripled home [[cb-illinois-cal-hejza|Cal Hejza]] and [[cb-illinois-cameron-chee-aloy|Cameron Chee-Aloy]]. [[cb-illinois-joey-rons|Joey Rons]] then finished two scoreless innings for the 8–6 win.
[[cb-florida-state-james-tibbs-iii|James Tibbs III]] went 4-for-6 with a home run and four RBI as Florida State held off Illinois 13–7 at Fluor Field.

Florida State opened a 7–0 lead through four innings behind [[cb-florida-state-daniel-cantu|Daniel Cantu]]’s RBI single, [[cb-florida-state-cam-smith|Cam Smith]]’s RBI double and two-run single, and Tibbs’ solo homer. Illinois answered with seven runs across the fourth, fifth and sixth to draw even.

With the game tied in the seventh, [[cb-florida-state-jaxson-west|Jaxson West]] drove a three-run double and [[cb-florida-state-alex-lodise|Alex Lodise]] added an RBI single. [[cb-florida-state-ben-barrett|Ben Barrett]] covered the final 3.2 innings without allowing a run, then Tibbs supplied two ninth-inning insurance RBI.
[[cb-winthrop-owen-sarna|Owen Sarna]] held Maine to two hits and one unearned run across five innings, striking out six as Winthrop rolled to a 15–4 win.

[[cb-winthrop-charlie-evans|Charlie Evans]] started a seven-run first with a leadoff homer and added a sacrifice fly later in the inning. [[cb-winthrop-jaylen-hernandez|Jaylen Hernandez]] doubled in a run, while [[cb-winthrop-anthony-ruocco|Anthony Ruocco]], [[cb-winthrop-harrison-wilson|Harrison Wilson]] and [[cb-winthrop-chazz-grossington|Chazz Grossington]] each drove in a run.

Winthrop added three more in the fourth when [[cb-winthrop-nicholas-badillo|Nicholas Badillo]] hit a two-run homer and Hernandez followed with a solo shot. Badillo finished with a homer and two RBI, and Hernandez went 2-for-2 with a double, homer and two RBI.
[[cb-virginia-henry-ford|Henry Ford]] led Virginia’s 26–12 win at George Washington, going 4-for-6 with two homers, four RBI and four runs scored.

Virginia erupted for four runs in the first, eight in the second and five in the fifth. [[cb-virginia-griff-oferrall|Griff O’Ferrall]] had three hits, a homer and four RBI, while [[cb-virginia-eric-becker|Eric Becker]] went 5-for-7 with two RBI and [[cb-virginia-jacob-ference|Jacob Ference]] collected three hits, two RBI and four runs.

George Washington scored 12 runs on 16 hits and held a 7–6 lead after four innings, but Virginia reclaimed control with its five-run fifth and never looked back. [[cb-virginia-ryan-osinski|Ryan Osinski]] earned the win with 2.1 innings of one-run relief.

[[cb-west-virginia-sam-white|Sam White]] went 2-for-3 with two RBI and two walks as West Virginia beat BYU, 10–4. His two-run single in the five-run fifth turned a one-run game into a 3–0 Mountaineers lead.

[[cb-west-virginia-skylar-king|Skylar King]] collected three hits and scored twice, while [[cb-west-virginia-ellis-garcia|Ellis Garcia]] singled home a run in the fifth and added a solo homer in the seventh. [[cb-west-virginia-kyle-west|Kyle West]] capped the fifth with a two-run single as West Virginia steadily built its margin.

BYU answered with home runs from [[cb-byu-cooper-vest|Cooper Vest]], [[cb-byu-kuhio-aloy|Kuhio Aloy]] and [[cb-byu-easton-jones|Easton Jones]], but could not catch up after West Virginia broke the game open with five runs in the fifth and three more in the seventh.

[[cb-virginia-tech-eddie-micheletti-jr|Eddie Micheletti Jr.]] went 3-for-4 with a double, a grand slam, five RBI and a walk as Virginia Tech opened ACC play with an 11–3 win over Notre Dame. His first-inning double helped the Hokies erase an early deficit, and his sixth-inning slam put the game away.

[[cb-virginia-tech-christian-martin|Christian Martin]] went 3-for-4 with two RBI and two runs, while [[cb-virginia-tech-chris-cannizzaro|Chris Cannizzaro]] supplied an RBI single in the opening rally. [[cb-virginia-tech-clay-grady|Clay Grady]] added three hits, including a triple, and drove in the final run.

[[cb-virginia-tech-brett-renfrow|Brett Renfrow]] earned the win with eight innings, allowing three hits and two earned runs while striking out 10. Notre Dame managed just three hits before [[cb-virginia-tech-jacob-exum|Jacob Exum]] finished the ninth with two strikeouts.

[[cb-binghamton-devan-bade|Devan Bade]]’s third-inning sacrifice fly gave Binghamton an early lead, but [[cb-vmi-cole-jenkins|Cole Jenkins]] put VMI ahead in the fifth with a two-run homer after [[cb-vmi-owen-prince|Owen Prince]] tied the game with an RBI single.

[[cb-binghamton-mike-gunning|Mike Gunning]] answered with a two-run homer in the sixth, scoring [[cb-binghamton-evin-sullivan|Evin Sullivan]] to tie the game at 3–3. [[cb-vmi-cole-garrett|Cole Garrett]] then supplied the decisive swing in the eighth, a two-run homer that brought home [[cb-vmi-tyler-swaim|Tyler Swaim]] and sent VMI to a 5–3 win.

[[cb-vmi-nathan-hawley|Nathan Hawley]] worked 2.1 scoreless innings with four strikeouts to earn the win, and [[cb-vmi-marcus-van-alstine|Marcus Van Alstine]] secured the final two outs for his fourth save. Sullivan finished 3-for-4 with a double for Binghamton.

[[cb-bucknell-andrew-swenson|Andrew Swenson]] went 3-for-4 with a double, a two-run homer, two RBI and two runs as Bucknell erupted for eight runs in the third inning. [[cb-bucknell-ryan-facinelli|Ryan Facinelli]] added a two-run double as the Bison raced from a 2–0 deficit to an 8–2 lead.

Campbell began its comeback when [[cb-campbell-grant-knipp|Grant Knipp]] hit a two-run homer in the fourth. The Camels scored four times in the fifth to tie it, helped by [[cb-campbell-trenton-harris|Trenton Harris]]’ error-assisted RBI bunt and [[cb-campbell-payton-howard|Payton Howard]]’ sacrifice fly, before taking the lead in the sixth on a passed ball.

[[cb-campbell-drew-siegner|Drew Siegner]] settled the game after the third-inning outburst, allowing three hits over 3.1 scoreless innings for the win. [[cb-campbell-packy-bradley-cooney|Packy Bradley-Cooney]] followed with three one-hit, scoreless innings and five strikeouts for his third save in Campbell’s 9–8 comeback.

[[cb-campbell-grant-knipp|Grant Knipp]] went 4-for-6 with three home runs, six RBI and four runs as Campbell overwhelmed Bucknell, 20–5. He hit a three-run homer in the third, then added solo and two-run blasts during a six-run seventh.

[[cb-campbell-dalen-thompson|Dalen Thompson]] hit two home runs and drove in four, including a first-inning two-run shot that started Campbell’s attack. [[cb-campbell-jonah-oster|Jonah Oster]] added a three-run homer in the second as the Camels collected eight home runs and 18 hits.

Bucknell briefly pulled within a run at 6–5 behind [[cb-bucknell-billy-kender|Billy Kender]]’s solo homer and [[cb-bucknell-michael-trommer|Michael Trommer]]’s three-run double, but Campbell scored 14 unanswered runs. [[cb-campbell-ethan-snyder|Ethan Snyder]] earned the win with 3.1 scoreless relief innings, and [[cb-campbell-nate-brittain|Nate Brittain]] struck out six over three scoreless innings for the save.

Rutgers jumped ahead 4–0 in the first inning, highlighted by [[cb-rutgers-jordan-durocher|Jordan Durocher]]’s two-run single. Durocher later stole second and reached third on an error as [[cb-rutgers-josh-kuroda-grauer|Josh Kuroda-Grauer]] stole home, before another RBI single completed the early surge.

[[cb-north-carolina-casey-cook|Casey Cook]] led North Carolina’s response with four hits and six RBI. His two-out, two-run double in the seventh snapped a 6–6 tie, and he added another two-run hit during the Tar Heels’ five-run eighth.

[[cb-north-carolina-vance-honeycutt|Vance Honeycutt]] went 4-for-5 with three runs and two RBI, while [[cb-north-carolina-gavin-gallaher|Gavin Gallaher]] and [[cb-north-carolina-colby-wilkerson|Colby Wilkerson]] each drove in a run in the decisive eighth. [[cb-north-carolina-matthew-matthijs|Matthew Matthijs]] earned the win with 1.2 scoreless innings as North Carolina completed its 13–7 comeback.

North Carolina answered Rutgers’ early scoring with seven runs through six innings, as [[cb-north-carolina-parks-harber|Parks Harber]] doubled home a first-inning run and [[cb-north-carolina-alberto-osuna|Alberto Osuna]] drove in two. The Tar Heels took a 7–3 lead when [[cb-north-carolina-casey-cook|Casey Cook]] and Harber scored on sixth-inning wild pitches.

Rutgers fought back with three runs in the seventh, including [[cb-rutgers-pete-durocher|Pete Durocher]]’s RBI double and two unearned runs on an outfield error. [[cb-north-carolina-luke-stevenson|Luke Stevenson]] answered in the eighth with a two-run homer that restored North Carolina’s three-run cushion.

[[cb-rutgers-jordan-sweeney|Jordan Sweeney]] brought Rutgers within one on a ninth-inning two-run homer, but [[cb-north-carolina-matt-poston|Matt Poston]] closed out the 9–8 win for his third save. [[cb-north-carolina-kyle-percival|Kyle Percival]] earned the victory with 2.1 innings of relief.

[[cb-georgia-tech-trey-yunger|Trey Yunger]] went 4-for-5 with two home runs, three RBI and four runs as Georgia Tech routed NC State, 15–5. He homered in each of the first two innings, then drove in another run during the Yellow Jackets’ five-run seventh.

[[cb-georgia-tech-matthew-ellis|Matthew Ellis]] went 2-for-3 with a two-run homer, three RBI, two runs and two walks. [[cb-georgia-tech-payton-green|Payton Green]] added two hits and three RBI, while [[cb-georgia-tech-mike-becchetti|Mike Becchetti]] scored three times and drove in two.

NC State’s [[cb-nc-state-jacob-cozart|Jacob Cozart]] hit a two-run double and [[cb-nc-state-alex-sosa|Alex Sosa]] followed with a two-run homer in the seventh, but Georgia Tech immediately answered with five runs. [[cb-georgia-tech-logan-mcguire|Logan McGuire]] earned the win by allowing two hits and one run over five innings with five strikeouts.

Louisville erased an early three-run deficit in the third, when [[cb-louisville-luke-napleton|Luke Napleton]] launched a game-tying grand slam. [[cb-louisville-dylan-hoy|Dylan Hoy]] followed with a two-run single in the fourth, pushing the Cardinals in front 7–5.

Wake Forest answered immediately. [[cb-wake-forest-mitchell-salvino|Mitchell Salvino]] scored on [[cb-wake-forest-adam-tellier|Adam Tellier]]’s RBI single before [[cb-wake-forest-seaver-king|Seaver King]] reached on an error that brought Tellier home, and the Deacs’ five-run seventh turned a one-run game into a six-run cushion.
Salvino owned the finish, going 3-for-4 with four runs and four RBIs, then drilling a three-run homer in the eighth to cap Wake Forest’s 16–7 comeback win.

[[cb-mercer-jackson-cherry|Jackson Cherry]] gave Mercer an early lead with a solo homer in the third, and [[cb-mercer-noah-best|Noah Best]] doubled home [[cb-mercer-parker-lester|Parker Lester]] in the sixth to make it 2–0.

The Bears added one run in each of the final three innings: [[cb-mercer-bradley-frye|Bradley Frye]] singled home [[cb-mercer-alex-ramirez|Alex Ramirez]] in the seventh, [[cb-mercer-carter-sanford|Carter Sanford]] drove in [[cb-mercer-conner-todaro|Conner Todaro]] in the eighth, and Todaro’s ninth-inning RBI single sent Lester home again.

[[cb-mercer-colton-cosper|Colton Cosper]] carried the shutout into the ninth and finished a complete game, allowing six hits with one walk and five strikeouts. [[cb-unc-greensboro-caleb-cozart|Caleb Cozart]]’s two-run homer provided UNCG’s late response, but Mercer closed out a 5–2 road win.

[[cb-vanderbilt-carter-holton|Carter Holton]] gave Vanderbilt six dominant innings, striking out 10 while holding South Carolina to two runs on three hits. The Gamecocks had used a two-out rally in the third—an RBI infield single and a bases-loaded walk—to take that initial 2–0 lead.

Vanderbilt tied it in the seventh when [[cb-vanderbilt-jack-bulger|Jack Bulger]] brought home [[cb-vanderbilt-rj-austin|RJ Austin]] on a groundout and [[cb-vanderbilt-jayden-davis|Jayden Davis]] followed with an RBI infield single. South Carolina then turned two Vanderbilt errors into five unearned runs in the bottom half.

[[cb-vanderbilt-matthew-polk|Matthew Polk]] hit a solo homer in the eighth and doubled home a ninth-inning run, but South Carolina held on for the 8–4 opener. [[cb-south-carolina-chris-veach|Chris Veach]] earned the win with 2.1 relief innings, and [[cb-south-carolina-garrett-gainey|Garrett Gainey]] closed for his third save.

Vanderbilt led 3–1 after four innings, using [[cb-vanderbilt-troy-laneve|Troy LaNeve]]’s RBI double, [[cb-vanderbilt-camden-kozeal|Camden Kozeal]]’s RBI single and [[cb-vanderbilt-rj-austin|RJ Austin]]’s run-scoring double. South Carolina had countered the first run on [[cb-south-carolina-ethan-petry|Ethan Petry]]’s solo homer in the second.

The Gamecocks broke through for four in the fifth. [[cb-south-carolina-tyler-causey|Tyler Causey]] doubled and scored on [[cb-south-carolina-blake-jackson|Blake Jackson]]’s double, [[cb-south-carolina-parker-noland|Parker Noland]] drove in Jackson with a groundout, and [[cb-south-carolina-cole-messina|Cole Messina]] followed with a two-run homer.

Petry and Causey supplied solo homers in the sixth, and Petry’s RBI single in the seventh finished South Carolina’s 8–3 sweep-clinching win. Petry went 3-for-3 with two homers, three RBIs and two runs, while [[cb-south-carolina-garrett-gainey|Garrett Gainey]] recorded a 2.1-inning save.

South Carolina broke the finale open with six first-inning runs, taking advantage of a pair of Vanderbilt errors before [[cb-south-carolina-dylan-brewer|Dylan Brewer]] connected for a two-run homer. The Gamecocks added a solo homer in the second and an RBI single in the third to build an 8–0 lead.

[[cb-vanderbilt-ryan-ginther|Ryan Ginther]] steadied Vanderbilt with two hitless relief innings, but South Carolina answered the Commodores’ seventh-inning rally with [[cb-south-carolina-kennedy-jones|Kennedy Jones]]’s solo homer and added two more runs on consecutive doubles in the eighth.

Vanderbilt finally scored in the seventh when [[cb-vanderbilt-matthew-polk|Matthew Polk]] singled home [[cb-vanderbilt-jayden-davis|Jayden Davis]] and [[cb-vanderbilt-jonathan-vastine|Jonathan Vastine]] plated [[cb-vanderbilt-troy-laneve|Troy LaNeve]]. [[cb-south-carolina-tyler-pitzer|Tyler Pitzer]] earned the 10–2 win with 6.1 innings, nine strikeouts and no earned runs.

William & Mary struck first in the second when [[cb-william-and-mary-josiah-seguin|Josiah Seguin]] singled home [[cb-william-and-mary-kevin-francella|Kevin Francella]] and [[cb-william-and-mary-luca-trigiani|Luca Trigiani]]. [[cb-william-and-mary-joe-delossantos|Joe Delossantos]] made it 3–0 with a solo homer in the fifth.

The Tribe put the game away in the seventh. Seguin was hit by a pitch, [[cb-william-and-mary-lucas-carmichael|Lucas Carmichael]] walked, and [[cb-william-and-mary-ben-parker|Ben Parker]] drove them both home with a three-run homer to left.

[[cb-william-and-mary-nate-knowles|Nate Knowles]] earned the win after 3.1 scoreless innings with six strikeouts, while Parker finished 3-for-5 with a homer and three RBIs. VCU scored once in the seventh and twice in the eighth, but William & Mary closed out a 6–3 road win.

Presbyterian opened with a first-inning RBI groundout, then added another run when [[cb-presbyterian-robbie-wallace|Robbie Wallace]] stole home in the third. The Blue Hose blew it open with four runs in the fifth.

[[cb-presbyterian-jayson-hugus|Jayson Hugus]] singled in two runs, then [[cb-presbyterian-ethan-lazio|Ethan Lazio]] followed with a two-run single to make it 6–0. Gardner-Webb scored in the seventh and ninth but could not recover.
[[cb-presbyterian-daniel-eagen|Daniel Eagen]] set the tone with five scoreless innings, allowing one hit and striking out 11. Presbyterian’s bullpen finished the 6–2 win with eight more strikeouts.

[[cb-liberty-todd-hudson|Todd Hudson]] gave Liberty all the offense it would need in the first inning, crushing a grand slam to right-center for an immediate 4–0 lead. The Flames added three more in the third on RBI doubles from [[cb-liberty-carson-foster|Carson Foster]] and [[cb-liberty-cameron-troyer|Cameron Troyer]].

Liberty widened the gap with two fourth-inning runs, then [[cb-liberty-brandon-horton|Brandon Horton]]’s RBI single in the eighth restored a five-run margin. Sam Houston scored in five separate innings but could not put together a larger rally.

[[cb-liberty-cole-hertzler|Cole Hertzler]] earned the win after six innings, allowing four runs—two earned—on seven hits. Hudson’s first-inning slam stood as the decisive swing in Liberty’s 10–5 victory.

Old Dominion led 2–0 after the first on [[cb-old-dominion-luke-waters|Luke Waters]]’ solo homer and Kyle Edwards’ steal of home. South Alabama got one back in the second when [[cb-south-alabama-jg-bell|JG Bell]] singled home Brennan Holt.

The Jaguars drew even on [[cb-south-alabama-joseph-sullivan|Joseph Sullivan]]’s RBI hit by pitch in the seventh, then took their first lead when [[cb-south-alabama-tyler-borges|Tyler Borges]] homered in the eighth. [[cb-south-alabama-will-turner|Will Turner]] added a ninth-inning solo shot, and Borges’ RBI single made it 5–2.

[[cb-south-alabama-seth-carter|Seth Carter]] earned the win with two scoreless innings, while [[cb-south-alabama-grant-wood|Grant Wood]] recorded the final two outs for his fifth save. Borges went 3-for-5 with a homer and two RBIs in South Alabama’s 5–3 comeback.

Coastal Carolina scored first on [[cb-coastal-carolina-cole-bodine|Cole Bodine]]’s RBI single, but UNCW answered in the second and went ahead in the third when [[cb-unc-wilmington-jac-croom|Jac Croom]] tripled home Bromley Thornton. Tanner Thach’s infield single brought Croom home on a throwing error.

A [[cb-unc-wilmington-bryan-arendt|Bryan Arendt]] solo homer stretched the Seahawks’ lead to 4–1 before Coastal pulled even in the sixth on [[cb-coastal-carolina-derek-bender|Derek Bender]]’s two-run single. UNCW immediately took back control in the seventh.

[[cb-unc-wilmington-aiden-evans|Aiden Evans]] doubled home Dylan Schaefer, and Croom followed with his second triple and second RBI. Croom finished 2-for-4 with two triples and two RBIs, while [[cb-unc-wilmington-luke-craig|Luke Craig]] retired the final 10 batters to secure the 6–4 win.

Virginia Tech stormed to a 7–0 lead through four innings, highlighted by [[cb-virginia-tech-carson-demartini|Carson DeMartini]]’s three-run homer in the first. Georgia Tech responded with six runs in the fifth to erase nearly all of the deficit.

The Yellow Jackets went ahead in the sixth as [[cb-georgia-tech-john-giesler|John Giesler]] homered, then added two more runs. [[cb-georgia-tech-payton-green|Payton Green]] helped drive the rally, going 3-for-4 with two RBIs as Georgia Tech scored 11 unanswered runs.

Georgia Tech added two eighth-inning insurance runs and [[cb-georgia-tech-dawson-brown|Dawson Brown]] recorded the final outs for his second save. The 11–7 comeback secured the series win over the No. 16 Hokies.

Southern Miss faced a 6–1 deficit after three innings despite [[cb-southern-mississippi-ozzie-pratt|Ozzie Pratt]]’s leadoff homer. The Golden Eagles began their comeback in the fifth when [[cb-southern-mississippi-carson-paetow|Carson Paetow]] hit a two-run homer.

[[cb-southern-mississippi-slade-wilks|Slade Wilks]] tied it with a two-run homer in the sixth, then [[cb-southern-mississippi-matthew-russo|Matthew Russo]]’s RBI single and [[cb-southern-mississippi-dalton-mcintyre|Dalton McIntyre]]’s two-run homer made it 8–6 in the seventh.

The Golden Eagles scored six more runs across the eighth and ninth, capped by [[cb-southern-mississippi-nick-monistere|Nick Monistere]]’s three-run single. [[cb-southern-mississippi-kros-sivley|Kros Sivley]] earned the win with six innings of relief, allowing three runs with six strikeouts in Southern Miss’ 14–9 rally.

[[cb-georgetown-owen-carapellotti|Owen Carapellotti]] put Georgetown ahead in the first inning with a three-run homer, bringing home [[cb-georgetown-christian-ficca|Christian Ficca]] and [[cb-georgetown-jake-hyde|Jake Hyde]] for an early 3–0 lead.
Connecticut answered with five runs in the fourth. [[cb-connecticut-maddix-dalena|Maddix Dalena]] delivered a two-run double, and the Huskies added two more in the fifth to take a 7–3 advantage.

Georgetown kept pressing, scoring once in the sixth and twice in the eighth to pull within a run. [[cb-connecticut-jack-sullivan|Jack Sullivan]] earned the win, while [[cb-connecticut-brady-afthim|Brady Afthim]] secured the final outs for his fifth save in Connecticut’s 7–6 victory.

Baylor struck first with two runs in the opening inning, including a leadoff homer by [[cb-gonzaga-enzo-apodaca|Enzo Apodaca]], but West Virginia answered with four in the bottom half and six more in the second to seize control.
