[[cb-west-virginia-jj-wetherholt|J.J. Wetherholt]] and [[cb-west-virginia-kyle-west|Kyle West]] each homered as the Mountaineers built a double-digit lead. [[cb-west-virginia-reed-chumley|Reed Chumley]] powered the offense with five RBIs during West Virginia’s 18-run outburst.

Baylor received two hits and two RBIs from [[cb-baylor-daniel-altman|Daniel Altman]], but West Virginia added five runs in the seventh to finish the scoring. [[cb-west-virginia-tyler-switalski|Tyler Switalski]] earned the win as the Mountaineers rolled 18–5.

[[cb-west-virginia-kyle-west|Kyle West]] opened the scoring with a second-inning solo homer, but Baylor tied it in the fourth when [[cb-baylor-cortlan-castle|Cortlan Castle]] singled home [[cb-baylor-hunter-teplanszky|Hunter Teplanszky]].

West Virginia answered with three fifth-inning runs. [[cb-west-virginia-sam-white|Sam White]] scored on a wild pitch before [[cb-west-virginia-grant-hussey|Grant Hussey]] and [[cb-west-virginia-brodie-kresser|Brodie Kresser]] delivered run-scoring outs; Kresser’s seventh-inning sacrifice bunt added the final insurance run.

[[cb-west-virginia-derek-clark|Derek Clark]] controlled the game for eight innings, allowing five hits and two runs while striking out eight. Teplanszky’s eighth-inning solo homer trimmed the margin, but [[cb-west-virginia-maxx-yehl|Maxx Yehl]] recorded the final out for the save in West Virginia’s 5–2 win.

George Washington struck first when [[cb-george-washington-ellis-schwartz|Ellis Schwartz]] singled home [[cb-george-washington-brett-young|Brett Young]] in the first, but Saint Louis erased the deficit with two runs in the third. [[cb-st-louis-drew-winters|Drew Winters]] doubled home [[cb-st-louis-easton-richter|Easton Richter]] before [[cb-st-louis-tyler-fogarty|Tyler Fogarty]] plated Winters with a groundout.

[[cb-st-louis-cole-smith|Cole Smith]] added a fourth-inning RBI groundout, while George Washington pulled within 3–2 on an unearned run in the bottom half. Smith’s sixth-inning sacrifice fly scored [[cb-st-louis-knox-preston|Knox Preston]] and restored Saint Louis’ two-run cushion.

[[cb-st-louis-owen-kelly|Owen Kelly]] earned the win with 4.2 innings of relief, yielding two hits and one unearned run while striking out four. [[cb-st-louis-evan-gray|Evan Gray]] followed with 2.1 scoreless innings and three strikeouts for the save as Saint Louis held on, 4–2.

Campbell struck first on [[cb-campbell-lawson-harrill|Lawson Harrill]]’s leadoff homer, but Liberty answered with five runs in the bottom of the first. [[cb-liberty-john-simmons|John Simmons]] cleared the bases with a three-run double, and [[cb-liberty-noah-rabon|Noah Rabon]] followed with an RBI single.

Harrill homered again in the third, but Simmons answered with a solo shot as Liberty rebuilt its lead. The Flames scored in every inning except the fifth, with Rabon finishing 2-for-4 with three RBIs and a stolen base.

Campbell rallied for four runs in the eighth and added a ninth-inning run, led by Harrill’s 4-for-5, two-homer performance. [[cb-liberty-trey-cooper|Trey Cooper]] earned the win as Liberty held off the Fighting Camels, 14–9.

[[cb-san-diego-logan-reddemann|Logan Reddemann]] controlled a scoreless pitchers’ duel for eight innings, allowing four hits, walking three and striking out nine. Santa Clara never advanced a runner home against the freshman right-hander.

San Diego broke through in the fifth when [[cb-san-diego-dustin-allen|Dustin Allen]] singled, moved up on [[cb-san-diego-joe-decriscio|Joe Decriscio]]’s sacrifice bunt and scored on [[cb-san-diego-will-worthington|Will Worthington]]’s RBI single.

Allen again set up Worthington in the seventh, reaching with a single before Decriscio’s base hit and a sacrifice advanced the runners. Worthington’s squeeze bunt plated Allen for the insurance run, and [[cb-san-diego-conner-thurman|Conner Thurman]] worked a scoreless ninth for the save in a 2–0 San Diego win.

USC opened a 2–0 first-inning lead on sacrifice flies from Jacob Galloway and Ethan Hedges, then added a sixth-inning run to pull within one. California’s staff answered with three shutout innings from [[cb-california-austin-turkington|Austin Turkington]] and a scoreless ninth from [[cb-california-tyler-stasiowski|Tyler Stasiowski]].

California turned the game in the fourth. [[cb-california-peyton-schulze|Peyton Schulze]] singled home [[cb-california-caleb-lomavita|Caleb Lomavita]], [[cb-california-seth-gwynn|Seth Gwynn]] tied the game with an RBI double, and [[cb-california-pj-moutzouridis|P.J. Moutzouridis]] followed with a two-run single for a 4–2 lead.

Schulze provided the decisive insurance in the eighth, lining a two-run single that brought home Lomavita and [[cb-california-jarren-advincula|Jarren Advincula]]. He finished 2-for-3 with three RBIs as [[cb-california-trey-newmann|Trey Newmann]] earned the win in California’s 6–3 series-clinching victory.

[[cb-miami-daniel-cuvet|Daniel Cuvet]] put Miami ahead immediately with a three-run first-inning homer, bringing home [[cb-miami-jacoby-long|Jacoby Long]] and [[cb-miami-edgardo-villegas|Edgardo Villegas]]. Louisville responded with an RBI double from [[cb-louisville-dylan-hoy|Dylan Hoy]] in the third and [[cb-louisville-jt-benson|J.T. Benson]]’s solo homer in the fifth.

Miami regained breathing room in the sixth when Lucas Costello homered and J.D. Urso singled home another run. Cuvet then delivered his second three-run shot in the seventh, again scoring Long and Villegas to extend the lead to 8–3.

Louisville made a ninth-inning push on [[cb-louisville-luke-napleton|Luke Napleton]]’s solo homer and [[cb-louisville-zion-rose|Zion Rose]]’s RBI double, but [[cb-miami-myles-caba|Myles Caba]] closed it out for the save. [[cb-miami-rafe-schlesinger|Rafe Schlesinger]] earned the win as Miami took the ACC Tournament opener, 8–5.

[[cb-florida-state-marco-dinges|Marco Dinges]] opened the ACC Tournament scoring with a two-run homer in the first, and Florida State built an 8–1 lead through five on two-run blasts by [[cb-florida-state-daniel-cantu|Daniel Cantu]], [[cb-florida-state-drew-faurot|Drew Faurot]] and [[cb-florida-state-jaime-ferrer|Jaime Ferrer]].

Georgia Tech surged back with five runs in the seventh. [[cb-georgia-tech-vahn-lackey|Vahn Lackey]] started the rally with an RBI double, while [[cb-georgia-tech-drew-burress|Drew Burress]], [[cb-georgia-tech-matthew-ellis|Matthew Ellis]], [[cb-georgia-tech-cam-jones|Cam Jones]] and [[cb-georgia-tech-mike-becchetti|Mike Becchetti]] each drove in a run to make it 8–6.

Florida State answered with four in the eighth, highlighted by Faurot’s RBI double and a two-run single from [[cb-florida-state-james-tibbs-iii|James Tibbs III]]. Georgia Tech drew within three again in the ninth, but [[cb-florida-state-jamie-arnold|Jamie Arnold]] struck out the tying run for his first save in the Seminoles’ 12–9 win.

Virginia Tech raced to a 5–0 lead in the second inning, but Duke batted around in the third to take control. [[cb-duke-zac-morris|Zac Morris]] hit a three-run homer, [[cb-duke-logan-bravo|Logan Bravo]] singled home a run, and [[cb-duke-chase-krewson|Chase Krewson]] followed with a two-run single to make it 6–5.

[[cb-duke-alex-stone|Alex Stone]] added a fifth-inning solo homer, then Morris delivered his second homer—a two-run shot in the sixth—to stretch the Blue Devils’ lead to 9–5. Bravo’s RBI double and [[cb-duke-wallace-clark|Wallace Clark]]’s run-scoring single made it 11–6 in the seventh.

Virginia Tech scored once in the seventh and twice in the eighth, but [[cb-duke-charlie-beilenson|Charlie Beilenson]] covered the final three innings for his 12th save, tying Duke’s single-season record. Morris finished 2-for-4 with two homers, five RBIs, two runs and a walk in Duke’s 11–8 comeback.

Virginia broke the game open with four runs in the second inning, then kept adding on in a seven-inning ACC Tournament shutout of Georgia Tech. [[cb-virginia-casey-saucke|Casey Saucke]] drove in a run during a 16-hit Cavalier attack, while [[cb-virginia-ethan-anderson|Ethan Anderson]] reached base four times and scored once.

[[cb-virginia-casey-saucke|Saucke]] delivered the biggest line, going 2-for-5 with a double, a home run and four RBIs. [[cb-virginia-henry-godbout|Henry Godbout]] homered, scored three times and stole a base, while [[cb-virginia-harrison-didawick|Harrison Didawick]] added a two-run homer as Virginia extended the margin in each of the fourth, fifth and sixth innings.

[[cb-tennessee-evan-blanco|Evan Blanco]] worked six scoreless innings for the win, scattering five hits with three strikeouts and one walk. [[cb-virginia-matt-augustin|Matt Augustin]] finished the seven-inning game with a hitless final inning.

Wake Forest seized control early against Pittsburgh in the ACC Tournament, with [[cb-wake-forest-jake-reinisch|Jake Reinisch]] launching a two-run homer in the first inning before [[cb-wake-forest-marek-houston|Marek Houston]] drilled a three-run shot in the second. The Demon Deacons carried that 5-0 lead to an 8-1 victory.

Pittsburgh got its only run on an RBI single from Jayden Melendez in the third, but [[cb-wake-forest-seaver-king|Seaver King]] answered with an RBI hit in the fifth. [[cb-wake-forest-cameron-gill|Cameron Gill]] homered in the sixth, and [[cb-wake-forest-tate-ballestero|Tate Ballestero]] added a pinch-hit RBI single in the seventh as Wake Forest pulled away.

[[cb-wake-forest-zach-johnston|Zach Johnston]] earned the win with two hitless relief innings, and Wake Forest's bullpen blanked Pittsburgh over the final seven frames. Houston's three-run homer supplied the decisive early swing.

NC State erupted for six runs in the third and four more in the fourth to bury Virginia Tech early in the ACC Tournament. [[cb-nc-state-alex-sosa|Alex Sosa]] cracked a three-run homer in the third, while [[cb-nc-state-alec-makarewicz|Alec Makarewicz]] supplied a two-run double in the next inning as the Wolfpack built a 10–0 lead.

Virginia Tech fought back with six runs in the sixth, highlighted by [[cb-virginia-tech-griffin-ebel|Griffin Ebel]]’s two-run double, but NC State answered with a run in the seventh and six more in the eighth. [[cb-nc-state-eli-serrano-iii|Eli Serrano III]] homered and [[cb-nc-state-brandon-butterworth|Brandon Butterworth]] went deep during the Wolfpack’s closing surge.

[[cb-nc-state-alec-makarewicz|Makarewicz]] finished a perfect 4-for-4 with four runs, four RBIs, a double and two walks. [[cb-nc-state-garrett-pennington|Garrett Pennington]] added four hits, four runs and three doubles in NC State’s 20-hit, 19–9 win.

Clemson took a 2–1 lead in the second on [[cb-clemson-jarren-purify|Jarren Purify]]’s two-run double, but Miami answered with five runs in the bottom half. [[cb-miami-antonio-jimenez|Antonio Jimenez]] drilled a three-run homer, then [[cb-miami-daniel-cuvet|Daniel Cuvet]] doubled home two more to put the Hurricanes in front for good.

Miami extended the margin on [[cb-miami-edgardo-villegas|Edgardo Villegas]]’s RBI single in the sixth and [[cb-miami-jake-kulikowski|Jake Kulikowski]]’s pinch-hit homer in the eighth. Clemson fought to the final out, as [[cb-clemson-cam-cannarella|Cam Cannarella]] tripled and [[cb-clemson-jimmy-obertop|Jimmy Obertop]] doubled during a two-run eighth before [[cb-clemson-jacob-hinderleider|Jacob Hinderleider]] homered in the ninth.

Jimenez went 2-for-3 with two runs, three RBIs and a walk, providing the game’s defining blow. Miami starter [[cb-miami-gage-ziehl|Gage Ziehl]] earned the win after allowing three runs, two earned, over six innings, and Myles Caba recorded the final six outs for the save in an 8–7 finish.

North Carolina opened the ACC Tournament game with four first-inning solo homers, as [[cb-north-carolina-anthony-donofrio|Anthony Donofrio]], [[cb-north-carolina-casey-cook|Casey Cook]], [[cb-north-carolina-parks-harber|Parks Harber]] and [[cb-north-carolina-alberto-osuna|Alberto Osuna]] all went deep. That immediate surge sent the Tar Heels toward a 12–2 win over Pittsburgh.

[[cb-north-carolina-anthony-donofrio|Donofrio]] added an RBI single in the fourth, then supplied the finishing blow with a three-run homer in the ninth. He reached base in all six plate appearances, going 3-for-3 with two homers, five RBIs, three runs and three walks; Cook also homered twice and drove in three.

Pittsburgh cut the margin to 5–2 in the fourth on C.J. Funk’s solo homer and Tyler Bischke’s RBI double, but [[cb-north-carolina-jason-decaro|Jason DeCaro]] held the Panthers there. DeCaro earned the win with seven innings of two-run ball, allowing five hits with six strikeouts.

Duke broke a scoreless game open with six runs in the fifth against NC State. [[cb-duke-chase-krewson|Chase Krewson]] started the barrage with a solo homer, [[cb-duke-zac-morris|Zac Morris]] followed with a grand slam, and [[cb-duke-aj-gracia|AJ Gracia]] added another solo shot.

[[cb-duke-devin-obee|Devin Obee]] extended the lead with a two-run homer in the sixth, giving Duke four home runs among its six hits. Morris drove in four on his fifth-inning blast, while Obee went 2-for-3 with two runs, two RBIs and a walk in the 8–1 victory.

[[cb-duke-andrew-healy|Andrew Healy]] set the tone on the mound, tossing five one-hit, scoreless innings with four strikeouts. James Tallon followed with two scoreless frames, and Tim Noone handled the final two innings as NC State’s only run came on a ninth-inning RBI double.

Florida State turned a one-run game into an 11–2 advantage with seven runs in the seventh inning against Virginia. [[cb-florida-state-james-tibbs-iii|James Tibbs III]] opened the scoring with a two-run single in the fourth, added an RBI walk in the fifth, and drove in another run with a sacrifice fly during the decisive seventh.

The Seminoles piled up the big inning behind RBI hits from [[cb-florida-state-marco-dinges|Marco Dinges]] and [[cb-florida-state-jaime-ferrer|Jaime Ferrer]], a two-run triple by [[cb-florida-state-daniel-cantu|Daniel Cantu]], an RBI double from [[cb-florida-state-alex-lodise|Alex Lodise]] and an RBI single by [[cb-florida-state-drew-faurot|Drew Faurot]]. Tibbs then homered in the eighth to finish with five RBIs.

Virginia answered with five seventh-inning runs on homers by Ethan Anderson, Luke Hanson and Casey Saucke, but [[cb-florida-state-brennen-oxford|Brennen Oxford]] held the Cavaliers to one run over the final three innings for the save. [[cb-florida-state-jamie-arnold|Jamie Arnold]] earned the win after six innings of two-run, nine-strikeout work in a 12–7 Florida State victory.

Louisville raced to a 6–0 lead through four innings, getting a first-inning homer from [[cb-louisville-jt-benson|JT Benson]], a two-run shot from [[cb-louisville-luke-napleton|Luke Napleton]] and two RBI doubles from [[cb-louisville-dylan-hoy|Dylan Hoy]]. The Cardinals still led 7–4 after an unearned run in the seventh.

Clemson rallied in the eighth when [[cb-clemson-jimmy-obertop|Jimmy Obertop]] launched a three-run homer to tie the game. [[cb-clemson-cam-cannarella|Cam Cannarella]] reached base five times and scored three runs, while [[cb-clemson-tristan-bissetta|Tristan Bissetta]] went 3-for-4 with a triple, two RBIs and a run during the comeback.

In the ninth, [[cb-clemson-jacob-hinderleider|Jacob Hinderleider]], [[cb-clemson-blake-wright|Blake Wright]] and Cannarella delivered consecutive singles to load the bases. Obertop drew the walk-off walk to force in Hinderleider, completing Clemson’s 8–7 win after Austin Gordon worked a perfect ninth for the victory.

James Madison built a 7–4 lead through six innings in the Raleigh Regional, powered by [[cb-james-madison-fenwick-trimble|Fenwick Trimble]]’s three-hit, three-RBI day. Trimble doubled home a run in the fifth and delivered a two-run double in the sixth after [[cb-james-madison-ryan-dooley|Ryan Dooley]] had driven in two with a single.

South Carolina chipped away with solo homers from Will Tippett and [[cb-south-carolina-kennedy-jones|Kennedy Jones]], then tied the game in the ninth when [[cb-south-carolina-cole-messina|Cole Messina]] hit a two-run homer. The Gamecocks had trailed by three entering the ninth.

In the 10th, Dylan Brewer scored the winning run on [[cb-south-carolina-will-tippett|Tippett]]’s sacrifice fly. [[cb-south-carolina-chris-veach|Chris Veach]] earned the win with 4.2 innings of two-run relief, and Messina reached base four times while supplying the game-tying swing in South Carolina’s 8–7 victory.

Bryant struck first on Jackson Phinney’s solo homer in the second, but NC State answered with three runs in the third. [[cb-nc-state-alec-makarewicz|Alec Makarewicz]] tied the game with an RBI double, [[cb-nc-state-brandon-butterworth|Brandon Butterworth]] followed with an RBI single, and [[cb-nc-state-luke-nixon|Luke Nixon]] added a sacrifice-bunt RBI.

The Wolfpack broke the game open with four runs in the sixth, keyed by [[cb-nc-state-noah-soles|Noah Soles]]’ two-run homer. Makarewicz added an RBI single and Butterworth another run-scoring hit, then Makarewicz doubled home a run in the eighth as NC State finished a 9–2 regional-opening win.

[[cb-nc-state-sam-highfill|Sam Highfill]] earned the win with six innings of two-run ball, yielding four hits with four strikeouts. [[cb-nc-state-jacob-dudan|Jacob Dudan]] retired the final nine Bryant batters in order and struck out six for the save, while Makarewicz went 4-for-5 with two doubles, three RBIs and two runs.

James Madison opened the Raleigh Regional with an 8–1 win over Bryant, jumping ahead on [[cb-james-madison-fenwick-trimble|Fenwick Trimble]]’s first-inning RBI double and a run-scoring single from Mike Schiavone. The Dukes nursed that two-run edge through five before turning the game into a rout late.

Kyle Entsminger set the tone on the mound, working 5.2 scoreless innings with seven strikeouts and no walks. Bryant collected eight hits but could not cash in until the eighth, when an error allowed its lone run to score.

James Madison added single runs in the sixth and seventh, then broke it open with four in the eighth. Mike Calabrese drove in two with a single, while Trevor O’Donnell and Josh Dunaway followed with RBI singles in the decisive inning.

NC State outlasted South Carolina 6–4 in the Raleigh Regional behind [[cb-nc-state-garrett-pennington|Garrett Pennington]]’s two-homer, three-RBI night. Pennington put the Wolfpack ahead with a first-inning solo shot, then restored the lead with a two-run homer in the third after [[cb-nc-state-eli-serrano-iii|Eli Serrano III]] had singled.

The Gamecocks kept answering: Will Tippett homered in the third, and [[cb-south-carolina-dylan-brewer|Dylan Brewer]] hit solo and two-run homers to tie the game at four in the seventh. [[cb-nc-state-cooper-consiglio|Cooper Consiglio]] earned the win in relief after allowing two runs over 2.1 innings.

NC State went back ahead in the bottom of the seventh when [[cb-nc-state-alex-sosa|Alex Sosa]] drew a bases-loaded walk. An eighth-inning throwing error after Pennington’s steal brought home the insurance run, and [[cb-nc-state-derrick-smith|Derrick Smith]] struck out four across 1.2 scoreless innings for the save.

[[cb-james-madison-mike-mancini|Mike Mancini]] supplied all the offense in James Madison’s 2–0 elimination-game win over South Carolina at the Raleigh Regional. He homered to right in the first inning, then drove a second solo shot to left in the eighth.

The Gamecocks put five runners on through the first five innings and received a double from Ethan Petry, but could not break through. [[cb-james-madison-ryan-dooley|Ryan Dooley]] was hit by a pitch and [[cb-james-madison-fenwick-trimble|Fenwick Trimble]] walked intentionally as the Dukes worked their own scoring chances around Mancini’s two swings.

Casey Smith covered the first 2.1 scoreless innings before Donovan Burke took over and shut the door. Burke allowed three hits and two walks over 6.2 scoreless innings, striking out seven to send James Madison on with the five-hit shutout.

Tampa opened the NCAA Division II Championship with a 9–3 win over Indianapolis behind [[cb-tampa-e-j-cumbo|E.J. Cumbo]]’s 4-for-5, three-RBI afternoon. Cumbo doubled and scored in the first, drove in a run with another double in the fourth, then capped his day with a two-run homer in the eighth.

Indianapolis briefly made it a one-run game in the fourth when Dakota Sill’s RBI single and a steal of home pulled the Greyhounds within 3–2. Tampa answered immediately on Cumbo’s RBI double, and the Greyhounds got no closer than 4–3 after Nick Lukac’s sixth-inning sacrifice bunt.

[[cb-tampa-j-p-gates|J.P. Gates]] broke the game open with a two-run homer in the seventh after an earlier sacrifice fly, finishing 3-for-4 with three RBIs. [[cb-tampa-alex-canney|Alex Canney]] earned the win with six innings of three-run ball and eight strikeouts before Gates and Eli Thurmond combined for three scoreless relief innings.

Angelo State erased an early three-run deficit and pulled away for a 13–6 NCAA Division II Championship win over Point Loma. [[cb-angelo-state-blake-wilhoite|Blake Wilhoite]] went 5-for-5 with two RBIs and two runs, beginning the comeback with a second-inning RBI single and adding another run-scoring hit in the eighth.

Point Loma led 5–2 after four innings on Joey Nicolai’s two-run homer, Bryson Hashimoto’s two-RBI day and Hunter Otjen’s RBI double. Angelo State answered immediately when [[cb-angelo-state-christian-garnette|Christian Garnette]] doubled home two, then took the lead for good in the sixth on Ryder McDaniel’s RBI single and Tripp Clark’s two-run double.

[[cb-angelo-state-kamden-kelton|Kamden Kelton]] scored three times and added two hits and two RBIs as Angelo State piled up six runs across the seventh and eighth. Johnny Stacy closed it with three scoreless innings and four strikeouts for the save after Mason Bryant earned the win in relief.

Florida rallied from a 4–2 deficit with seven runs in the fifth inning to beat Clemson 10–7 in Game 1 of the Super Regional. [[cb-florida-jac-caglianone|Jac Caglianone]] supplied the pivotal swing, a three-run homer that put the Gators in front after Cade Kurland and Michael Robertson had reached.

[[cb-florida-luke-heyman|Luke Heyman]] followed with an RBI single, Dale Thomas and Brody Donay added run-producing plays, and Robertson capped the inning with an RBI single. Clemson cut the margin to 9–7 with two sixth-inning runs, but Florida’s bullpen did not permit another run.

[[cb-florida-brandon-neely|Brandon Neely]] struck out seven over four scoreless innings for the save after [[cb-florida-fisher-jameson|Fisher Jameson]] earned the win in relief. Heyman added a ninth-inning homer, finishing 2-for-5 with two RBIs, while Caglianone went 2-for-4 with the homer, three RBIs and a walk.

Barton used a three-run second and a five-run fourth to roll past Lenoir-Rhyne 10–4. [[cb-barton-jerry-guzman|Jerry Guzman]] went 3-for-3 with two RBIs, two runs and a walk, delivering a two-run single in the second before an error-assisted bunt single helped start the fourth-inning outburst.

Salvatore Laimo doubled in a run during the early surge, and Barton kept moving the line in the fourth. [[cb-barton-yariel-diaz|Yariel Diaz]] walked in a run, Gavin Gilmore singled home another, Chase Waddell supplied a sacrifice fly and Mason Staz capped the inning with an RBI double.

[[cb-barton-a-j-campbell|A.J. Campbell]] earned the win with six scoreless innings, allowing four hits while striking out six. Lenoir-Rhyne scored once in the seventh and three times in the ninth, but Barton’s early 9–0 advantage was more than enough.

Georgia opened its 2025 season with a 9–1 win over Quinnipiac at Brooks Field, scoring five runs in the first inning despite producing only four hits for the game. [[cb-unc-asheville-robbie-burnett|Robbie Burnett]] scored three times and reached base four times, while Ryland Zaborowski’s three-run double provided the first-inning knockout blow.

[[cb-duke-devin-obee|Devin Obee]] drove in three runs with a first-inning walk, a sixth-inning solo homer and a sacrifice fly in the seventh. Burnett’s seventh-inning RBI double and Obee’s sacrifice fly made it 9–1 after Quinnipiac had briefly scored in the third.

Zach Harris worked four innings, allowing one run on three hits, before Paul Farley covered the final five frames for the win. Farley permitted only one hit and no runs while striking out three, finishing the staff’s one-run, four-hit effort.

[[cb-unc-wilmington-zane-taylor|Zane Taylor]] made UNCW’s opener a pitching clinic, holding Quinnipiac to three hits without a walk over 7.2 innings and striking out nine. [[cb-quinnipiac-sebastian-mueller|Sebastian Mueller]] supplied the Bobcats’ only run with a fourth-inning solo homer.

UNCW broke through for five runs in the second. [[cb-unc-wilmington-tanner-thach|Tanner Thach]] delivered the decisive swing, a three-run homer after RBI plays from Bryan Arendt and Aidan Evans, while an error made the latter three runs unearned.

The Seahawks added three in the sixth on Mac Gillespie’s two-run single and Martin Zelenka’s RBI single, then finished the 12–1 result with four in the eighth. Thach went 2-for-5 with two runs and three RBI, Brock Wills finished 3-for-4 with two runs, and Taylor earned the win.

Georgia seized a 2–0 first-inning lead without a hit, loading the bases on two walks and a hit batter before [[cb-georgia-slate-alford|Slate Alford]] walked in a run and [[cb-duke-devin-obee|Devin Obee]] lifted a sacrifice fly. Quinnipiac responded with three in the fourth, using RBI singles from Christian Smith and Sean McCulloch around a Georgia error.

[[cb-georgia-nolan-mccarthy|Nolan McCarthy]] tied the game with an RBI triple in the sixth, and Georgia reclaimed the lead in the seventh when [[cb-georgia-ryland-zaborowski|Ryland Zaborowski]] singled home Alford. Quinnipiac answered with Kyle Garbowski’s RBI groundout in the bottom half, sending the game to the eighth tied 4–4.

[[cb-unc-asheville-robbie-burnett|Robbie Burnett]]’s RBI single put Georgia ahead for good in the eighth, and Alford followed with a two-run single for a 7–4 final. Alford went 1-for-2 with three RBI and three walks; [[cb-georgia-state-davis-chastain|Davis Chastain]] earned the win, and DJ Radtke worked two scoreless innings for the save.

[[cb-georgia-henry-hunter|Henry Hunter]] opened Georgia’s scoring with a fourth-inning RBI single, then drove in another run as the Bulldogs broke a 3–3 tie with three in the seventh. He finished 2-for-4 with three RBI, while [[cb-georgia-nolan-mccarthy|Nolan McCarthy]] went 3-for-4, doubled and scored twice.

UNCW answered Georgia’s two-run fourth with RBI singles from Brock Wills and Kevin Jones, then pulled even in the sixth on Alec DeMartino’s solo homer. Tre Phelps put Georgia back ahead with a fifth-inning RBI single before the decisive seventh-inning rally.

[[cb-georgia-alton-davis-ii|Alton Davis II]] earned the win in relief, striking out seven while allowing one run over 3.2 innings. Georgia added an eighth-inning RBI walk from Hunter and [[cb-duke-devin-obee|Devin Obee]] drove in a run on a hit by pitch as the Bulldogs finished a 7–3 win.

UNCW built a 3–0 lead behind first-inning RBI plays from Cole Nelson and Kevin Jones, then Aidan Evans’ fourth-inning groundout. Quinnipiac fought back with three sixth-inning runs, using RBI plays from [[cb-quinnipiac-sebastian-mueller|Sebastian Mueller]], CJ Willis and Alex Irizarry to tie the game.

Quinnipiac moved ahead with two runs in the ninth on [[cb-quinnipiac-james-marino|James Marino]]’s RBI double and [[cb-quinnipiac-gabe-wright|Gabe Wright]]’s run-scoring single, but UNCW answered with Trevor Lucas’ RBI double and a bases-loaded hit-by-pitch to force extras.

The Bobcats blew it open with five in the 10th, scoring on Wright’s sacrifice fly and four bases-loaded walks. Marino finished 2-for-2 with two runs and an RBI, while [[cb-quinnipiac-j-c-franconere|J.C. Franconere]] earned the win and [[cb-quinnipiac-johnny-knox|Johnny Knox]] recorded the save in the 10–6 victory.

UNCW struck for six runs in the first, beginning with [[cb-unc-wilmington-trevor-lucas|Trevor Lucas]]’ sacrifice fly and continuing with Ryker Galaska’s RBI hit by pitch, Kevin Jones’ RBI single and [[cb-unc-wilmington-bryan-arendt|Bryan Arendt]]’s two-run double. A wild pitch brought home the sixth run.

[[cb-unc-wilmington-connor-marshburn|Connor Marshburn]] made the lead stand up with six no-hit innings, walking two and striking out seven. Georgia did not record a hit until [[cb-duke-devin-obee|Devin Obee]] homered in the eighth; Slate Alford later drove in the Bulldogs’ other run on a hit by pitch.

Georgia’s bullpen combined to allow only one hit after the opening inning, with JT Quinn striking out four in two frames and Tyler McLoughlin three more in two. But UNCW’s opening barrage and Marshburn’s start carried the Seahawks to a 6–2 win.

[[cb-washington-cooper-whitton|Cooper Whitton]] put Washington ahead in the second with a two-run single, but Saint Joseph’s answered with Owen Petrich’s two-run double in the third. Washington regained the lead in the fourth on RBI hits from [[cb-washington-sam-decarlo|Sam DeCarlo]] and [[cb-washington-colton-bower|Colton Bower]], only to see the Hawks tie it again on Joey Gale’s sixth-inning RBI double.

Washington broke the game open with three unearned runs in the seventh, capped by Malakhi Knight’s RBI walk and a run on a wild pitch. Bower added a solo homer in the eighth, then Whitton’s RBI double and Casen Taggart’s two-run homer drove a four-run ninth that made it 12–4.

Saint Joseph’s rallied for five in the ninth, including Carson Applegate’s two-run homer, but [[cb-washington-josh-emanuals|Josh Emanuels]] recorded the final out for the save. Whitton went 2-for-4 with a double and three RBI, while Isaac Yeager earned the win with 2.2 innings of one-run relief.

[[cb-coastal-carolina-jacob-morrison|Jacob Morrison]] set the tone with four scoreless innings, allowing two hits and striking out six as Coastal Carolina built a 3–0 lead. Walker Mitchell singled in the first run of the second, Dean Mihos added a sacrifice fly, and Sebastian Alexander’s fifth-inning single drove in another.

Kansas State got on the board in the sixth when Nick English scored on a failed pickoff, but Coastal responded with four runs. [[cb-coastal-carolina-ty-barrango|Ty Barrango]] hit a solo homer, Caden Bodine added an RBI single, and Domenico Tozzi doubled home two.

Coastal added two more in the seventh and finished with 14 hits in a 9–2 win. Bodine went 3-for-5 with an RBI, Tozzi was 3-for-5 with two RBI, and Morrison earned the victory before the bullpen limited Kansas State to two runs.

Kennesaw State raced to a 4–0 lead through two innings, getting a sacrifice fly from Cooper Williams, an RBI single from Shamaar McDuffie and Chris Cole’s two-run triple. Georgia began its comeback in the fourth, with [[cb-georgia-ryland-zaborowski|Ryland Zaborowski]]’s RBI single and a wild pitch cutting the deficit in half.

[[cb-georgia-slate-alford|Slate Alford]] tied the game with a seventh-inning solo homer, and Ryan Black’s solo shot in the eighth put Georgia in front for the first time. Black finished 2-for-3 with two runs, two RBI and two walks, while Alford went 2-for-4 with two runs, a homer and an RBI.

Georgia added two insurance runs in the ninth on a wild pitch and Black’s RBI single. [[cb-georgia-tyler-mcloughlin|Tyler McLoughlin]] earned the win with a clean inning and two strikeouts, and Brian Curley struck out two in the ninth for the save in a 6–4 comeback.

North Alabama jumped ahead in the first when Jonathan Lane singled and Nash Rippen followed with a two-run homer. Auburn answered immediately as Deric Fabian’s RBI single scored Ike Irish, then [[cb-auburn-chris-rembert|Chris Rembert]] tied it with a solo homer in the fifth.

The Tigers moved in front for good in the sixth. Eric Snow singled, advanced on an error and scored on [[cb-auburn-bub-terrell|Bub Terrell]]’s RBI double; Auburn then put three more across in the eighth, with Snow’s RBI single and Terrell’s RBI groundout extending the margin.

Auburn’s relief corps shut the door after the early deficit. [[cb-auburn-griffin-graves|Griffin Graves]] earned the win with a scoreless sixth, and Parker Carlson worked the final three innings without allowing a hit, striking out five for the save in a 6–2 victory.

Troy built an early cushion at Riddle-Pace Field, scoring on Dillon Kuehl’s first-inning RBI single before Sean Darnell drilled a three-run homer in the second. [[cb-troy-brooks-bryan|Brooks Bryan]] singled in the first and later came home on Kuehl’s two-run double as the Trojans stretched the lead to seven.

Northwestern State broke through with two runs in the sixth on Braden Benton’s RBI double and Clay Jung’s RBI single, but Troy answered with two more in the bottom half. Drew Nelson earned the win after allowing two runs over 5.2 innings, and the Trojans had built a 9–2 lead before the final frame.

Rocco Gump’s two-run single cut the deficit to five in the seventh, only for [[cb-troy-brooks-bryan|Bryan]] to answer with a grand slam. Peyton Watts added an RBI single as Troy finished a 14–4, seven-inning win; Bryan went 3-for-5 with a homer and four RBI, while Darnell scored four runs and drove in three.

UT Martin seized a 6–1 lead through two innings, beginning with Brody Capps’ two-run homer and Arderrius Townsend’s solo shot before Jonah Katsaboulas drove in two more. Middle Tennessee chipped back on Eston Snider’s RBI single, Matt Wolfe’s sacrifice fly and solo homers from Nathan Brewer and Brett Rogers to tie the game in the third.

The Skyhawks surged back in front with five runs in the seventh, capped by Garner Anderson’s grand slam, and carried an 11–6 lead into the eighth. [[cb-middle-tennessee-brett-vondohlen|Brett Vondohlen]] answered with a game-tying grand slam, then Kenny McKinley followed with a solo homer for Middle Tennessee’s first lead.

Anderson’s RBI single tied it again in the ninth, but [[cb-middle-tennessee-brett-vondohlen|Vondohlen]] led off the 10th with his second homer of the day to end it. Vondohlen finished 2-for-6 with two homers and five RBI, while Landen Burch earned the win with 0.2 scoreless innings in the 13–12 walk-off.

Old Dominion took an early 2–0 lead on Kainen Jorge’s first-inning sacrifice fly and an error-assisted fourth-inning run. St. Bonaventure answered in the bottom of the fourth when Mike Gunning’s sacrifice fly brought Jayce Tharnish home.

[[cb-st-bonaventure-conner-vercollone|Conner Vercollone]] turned the game in the fifth, launching a three-run homer after Harrison Kaufman walked and Morgan Little singled. Old Dominion pulled within a run in the sixth on Efrain Morales’ sacrifice fly, then Kyle Edwards’ eighth-inning RBI single tied the game at 4–4.

The Bonnies loaded the bases in the bottom of the eighth, and Antonio Cordeiro’s walk forced in the go-ahead run before Little lined a two-run single for the final margin. [[cb-st-bonaventure-luke-roggenburk|Luke Roggenburk]] earned the win with four innings of one-run relief and six strikeouts in St. Bonaventure’s 7–4 victory.

Old Dominion and UT Martin traded zeroes for seven innings, with Old Dominion starter Dylan Brown striking out seven across six scoreless frames. [[cb-ut-martin-drake-bayles|Drake Bayles]] matched him for UT Martin, working seven scoreless innings while allowing four hits, walking four and striking out five.

The Skyhawks finally broke through in the eighth. Jalen Fithian singled, Garner Anderson was hit by a pitch and TJ Grines dropped a bunt single to load the bases; Brody Capps then drew an RBI walk before Jonah Katsaboulas drove in two with a single.

JT Popick added an RBI groundout and Frank Micallef singled in the fifth run of the inning, then Grines’ ninth-inning groundout provided the final run. Mason Shropshire retired all six hitters he faced in relief as UT Martin finished the 6–0 shutout.

St. Bonaventure raced to a 7–0 lead through three innings, taking advantage of Middle Tennessee errors before Antonio Cordeiro’s two-run double, Jayce Tharnish’s RBI single and Chris Hoalcraft’s two RBI hits. [[cb-st-bonaventure-conner-vercollone|Conner Vercollone]] added an RBI single in the third as the Bonnies kept extending the opening burst.

Harrison Kaufman hit a fifth-inning solo homer, and Hoalcraft drove in another run in the inning to make it 9–0. Middle Tennessee finally scored in the fifth on Kenny McKinley’s RBI groundout, but the Bonnies answered with three in the sixth behind a Kaufman sacrifice fly, Vercollone’s RBI single and Tharnish’s bases-loaded walk.

[[cb-st-bonaventure-michael-salina|Michael Salina]] controlled the game for six innings, allowing three hits and one unearned run while striking out nine. St. Bonaventure added its 13th run on Kaufman’s seventh-inning sacrifice fly and completed the 13–3, seven-inning victory.

Middle Tennessee struck first on [[cb-middle-tennessee-brett-vondohlen|Brett Vondohlen]]’s first-inning solo homer and Nathan Brewer’s error-assisted RBI single. Old Dominion responded in the second when Zach Leite doubled home Kainen Jorge, then drew even in the fourth on Leite’s steal of second and a throwing error that allowed Jorge to score.

The Monarchs moved ahead with two fifth-inning runs, as Luke Waters singled in Kyle Edwards and Leite added another RBI single. Edwards stole third and came home on another throwing error in the sixth, giving Old Dominion a 5–2 lead before Vondohlen’s eighth-inning RBI single trimmed the margin.

[[cb-old-dominion-blake-morgan|Blake Morgan]] earned the win with 7.2 innings, allowing three runs on eight hits while striking out seven. Kellen Davis and Bailey Matela finished the final four outs, with Matela recording the save in the 5–3 Old Dominion victory.

St. Bonaventure and UT Martin traded early runs, with Mike Gunning’s RBI single answered by Brody Capps’ solo homer. UT Martin briefly moved in front in the third on Garner Anderson’s RBI double and an error, but St. Bonaventure tied it when Paul Vossen stole third and scored on a throwing error.

The Bonnies broke the game open with five runs in the fifth. [[cb-st-bonaventure-conner-vercollone|Conner Vercollone]] singled home Gunning, Jayce Tharnish added a two-run single, and a two-run error-assisted Hoalcraft play made it 8–4. David Marshall’s seventh-inning RBI single stretched the lead to six.

Vercollone added a sacrifice fly in the ninth and finished 2-for-5 with two RBI and two runs, while Vossen scored four times. [[cb-st-bonaventure-kade-walker|Kade Walker]] earned the win with two innings of one-run relief as St. Bonaventure completed a 13–6 victory.
